The last stage answers a question the query design raises: *which vector represents a gene, and how does a query become a scalar?* DeepSpotM answers both with biological priors from five foundation-model modalities.

### Multi-source gene embeddings

`MultiSourceGeneEmbedding` holds, per source: a trainable `(n_genes, bio_dim_i)` gene-token parameter initialized from the source's pre-computed embeddings, and a trainable adapter (`Linear(bio_dim_i → 256) + LayerNorm`) projecting it into the cross-attention query space. A frozen one-hot **modality encoding** (dna / rna / protein / single_cell / text) is added to every query so the shared attention always knows which modality of prior it is being asked about. Sources dispatch at *runtime* through an `active_source` attribute — the module is one object that behaves as eleven different gene vocabularies' worth of priors:

| Source | Modality |
|---|---|
| `evo2` | dna |
| `orthrus` | rna |
| `prott5`, `esm2` | protein |
| `scgpt`, `geneformer`, `geneformer_cancer` | single_cell |
| `apertus`, `genept_ada`, `genept_m3` | text |
| `string_network` | *(no modality mapping — requires `use_modality_encoding=False`)* |

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L148-L181), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L71-L92), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L458-L470)

> [!TIP]
> `active_source` is a plain Python attribute, deliberately **not** part of the state dict — it does not survive a checkpoint round-trip. Any freshly loaded multi-source model must call `set_source(name)` (or `from_pretrained(..., source=...)`) before its first forward, or the decoder raises at query construction.

### The router: weights generated per gene

Instead of a shared `Linear(256, 1)` output head, the default configuration uses `GeneRouter`, a hypernetwork whose two MLPs take a gene's biological embedding `(G, bio_dim)` and *generate* that gene's projection: a 256-d weight vector and a scalar bias. Expression is then `einsum('bgd,gd->bg', queries, proj) + bias`. Because the weights are a function of the embedding rather than a fixed parameter, providing embeddings for an unseen gene at inference makes it zero-shot predictable — there is simply no per-gene parameter to be missing.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L110-L145), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L761-L785)

> [!TIP]
> In multi-source mode the router reads `current_bio.detach()` — the gradient reaches the bio parameter only through the adapter (query) pathway. The comment records why: without the detach, the bio tensor would be co-optimized by three consumers (adapter, router weight-net, router bias-net) simultaneously, which measurably destabilized validation Pearson correlation.

The router's internals and the "same embedding feeds adapter + router" invariant are expanded in [Gene Router Hypernetwork](10-gene-router-hypernetwork); the source/adapter/modality machinery in [Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings).

## Vocabulary as an Architectural Contract

Every shape above depends on `G`, and `G` is owned by `StructureExpression`: it reads `tokens.csv` (bundled via `config.py`), filters `token_type == 'gene'` rows, and fixes the ordered gene panel. `DeepSpotM.__init__` copies that ordering into `self.gene_names`, so **output column i is always `model.gene_names[i]`** — the mapping from prediction vector back to gene symbols never re-parses the CSV. The same class converts per-sample `{gene: value}` dicts into `(tensor, mask)` pairs for training, expecting upstream-normalized values (e.g. log1p CPM).

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L17-L39), [config.py](src/deepspotm/config.py#L1-L20), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L66-L77)

Crucially, the vocabulary is swappable at runtime: `swap_gene_vocabulary` rebuilds the vocab-shaped layers (`gene_embeddings`, query projection, router) against a new embedding tensor and gene list — the mechanism that lets a checkpoint trained on one panel serve another. This shapes the persistence layer too: `VOCAB_SPECIFIC_PREFIXES` names exactly those vocab-sized keys so they can be filtered out before loading a cross-vocabulary checkpoint.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L126-L165), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L18-L22)

Details live in [Gene Vocabulary and Output Mapping](12-gene-vocabulary-and-output-mapping) and [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling).

## Configuration Surface: Everything Is an Ablation Switch

The `DeepSpotM.__init__` signature is the architecture's honest spec: every design decision is a hyperparameter, and all of them are persisted via `save_hyperparameters` so checkpoints reconstruct their exact structure. The released model is the default column below:

| Hyperparameter | Default | Governs |
|---|---|---|
| `encoder_model` | `"MidnightEncoder"` | Vision backbone (registry key) |
| `use_lora` / `r` | `True` / `8` | PEFT wrapping (α = 2r, dropout 0.2) vs. frozen backbone |
| `use_cross_attention` | `True` | Query decoder vs. MLP fallback head |
| `gene_embed_dim` | `256` | Shared decoder width (`patch_proj`, queries, router output) |
| `cross_attn_layers` / `heads` | `2` / `8` | Decoder depth and attention breadth |
| `init_gene_embeddings` | `"xavier"` | `"xavier"` random init, one source name, or a list → multi-source mode |
| `use_router` | `True` | Hypernetwork head vs. shared `Linear(256, 1)` |
| `use_modality_encoding` | `True` | Frozen one-hot modality signal on queries |
| `token_path` | `None` | Custom vocabulary override |
| `backbone_pretrained` / `bio_dims` | `True` / `None` | Set by `from_pretrained`: offline architecture build + shape-only parameter allocation |

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L39-L117)

Two defaults are worth reading as architecture: setting `use_cross_attention=False` swaps the entire decoder for a plain `Linear(hidden_dim → 256) → GELU → Linear(256 → n_genes)` head over pooled backbone features — the non-query baseline this model was compared against. And passing `init_gene_embeddings` as a *list* is the switch that activates the multi-source stack (per-source bio params, adapters, routers); a single name builds the legacy single-source path. Note also that `bio_dims` lets checkpoint loading allocate decoder parameters purely from shapes recorded in `config.json`, without touching the raw gene-embedding `.pt` assets.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L97-L117), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L522-L560)

## Persistence Architecture: Self-Contained Reconstruction

The loading layer is designed around one invariant: *a checkpoint must rebuild the model that produced it, without external assets or network access.* `from_pretrained` fetches only three files (`config.json`, `model.safetensors`, `tokens.csv`) from HuggingFace or a local directory, rebuilds the architecture from saved hyperparameters (with `backbone_pretrained=False`), and loads the baked-in weights — backbone, LoRA adapters, and decoder together. `load_for_inference(source=...)` is the memory-efficient variant: it overrides `init_gene_embeddings` to just the named source so only one ~gene-embedding bank and adapter are ever constructed, then `strict=False`-loads and silently drops the other four sources' tensors (~750 MB on disk across the five default sources).

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L249-L314), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L188-L247)

Loading drift is never silent: `check_state_dict_load` fails loudly if any missing/unexpected key falls outside an explicit allow-list, and `from_pretrained` filters only PEFT bookkeeping from its "missing" report. This persistence layer is intentionally thin here — the mechanics have their own pages: [Pretrained Model Loading](13-pretrained-model-loading), [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling), [Memory-Efficient Source Loading](15-memory-efficient-source-loading).

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L56-L82), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L290-L314)

## Design Principles at a Glance

Four principles recur across every component above, and they explain most of the code's otherwise surprising structure:

1. **Genes as queries** — the decoder is gene-symmetric, which buys zero-shot genes, subsetting-as-acceleration, and per-gene attention maps from one design choice.
2. **Hypernetworked output** — per-gene weights are *generated* from biological embeddings, so capacity follows the prior rather than a parameter table.
3. **Runtime, not state-dict, dispatch** — source selection (`active_source`) and LoRA wrapping exist outside the persisted weights; the API makes setting them explicit and load-time code reconstructs them deterministically.
4. **Everything toggles, nothing drifts silently** — every architectural choice is an `__init__` hyperparameter; loading asserts full state-dict accounting and vocab-shaped layers are rebuilt, never shape-mismatched.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L11-L37), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L110-L145), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L148-L181), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L56-L82)

## Where to Go Next

With the system map in place, the Deep Dive pages explore each stage in dependency order: start with the vision stage in [Pathology Vision Encoders](7-pathology-vision-encoders) and its adaptation mechanism in [LoRA Adaptation Contract](8-lora-adaptation-contract); then the head in [Cross-Attention Gene Decoder](9-cross-attention-gene-decoder), [Gene Router Hypernetwork](10-gene-router-hypernetwork), and [Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings). If you are here to run the released model rather than study it, jump directly to [Pretrained Model Loading](13-pretrained-model-loading) or the hands-on [TCGA-SKCM Tutorial Notebook](4-tcga-skcm-tutorial-notebook).

# Pathology Vision Encoders



This page explains the vision encoder layer of DeepSpotM — the component that converts histology image tiles into the embeddings consumed by the gene prediction heads. It covers the encoder class hierarchy, the seven supported pathology foundation models, the two output pooling contracts, weight resolution behavior, and the exact integration points where `DeepSpotM` consumes the encoder. Deep dives into LoRA fine-tuning mechanics, the cross-attention decoder, and transform internals are deferred to their dedicated pages.

## Role in the Architecture

The vision encoder is the first stage of every DeepSpotM inference path. `DeepSpotM` instantiates it through a name-based factory, optionally wraps it in PEFT LoRA adapters, and then calls one of two methods depending on which gene prediction head is active: the spatial-token path (`forward_patch_tokens`) feeds the Cross-Attention Gene Decoder, while the pooled-vector path (`forward`) feeds a fallback MLP head. Each encoder also owns its own image transform pipeline, because every foundation model was pretrained with a different normalization scheme.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T["Histology tile"] --> P["Encoder-owned transforms<br/>(NORM_MEAN / NORM_STD)"]
    P --> E["Vision backbone<br/>(ViT foundation model)"]
    E -->|"forward_patch_tokens<br/>(B, N_patches, D)"| XA["Cross-attention gene decoder"]
    E -->|"forward<br/>(B, hidden_dim)"| MLP["MLP gene head"]
    XA --> G["Gene expression vector"]
    MLP --> G
```

Which branch is taken is decided in `DeepSpotM.forward`: when `use_cross_attention=True` (the default) the backbone's spatial patch tokens feed the decoder; otherwise the pooled embedding feeds the MLP head. This dual-contract design is the central reason the encoder API exposes two differently-shaped outputs.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L370-L391), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L97-L117)

## Class Hierarchy and the Encoder Contract

All encoders derive from the abstract `ImageEncoder` base class, which defines the interface every backbone must satisfy. Two intermediate strategies exist: `_TimmEncoder` factors out the shared build pipeline for timm-based vision transformers, while `ImageCLIPEncoder` and `MidnightEncoder` implement HuggingFace `transformers`-based construction directly.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ImageEncoder {
        <<abstract>>
        +LORA_TARGET_MODULES
        +NORM_MEAN
        +NORM_STD
        +forward(x)*
        +_build(weights_path)*
        +forward_patch_tokens(pixel_values)
        +set_transforms(**kwargs)
        +patch_dim
    }
    class _TimmEncoder {
        <<abstract>>
        +TIMM_NAME
        +TIMM_KWARGS
        +HF_REPO_ID
        +HF_FILENAME
        +HIDDEN_DIM
        +POOLING
    }
    class UNI1Encoder
    class UNI2Encoder
    class H0miniEncoder
    class H0Encoder
    class H1Encoder
    class ImageCLIPEncoder
    class MidnightEncoder

    ImageEncoder <|-- _TimmEncoder
    ImageEncoder <|-- ImageCLIPEncoder
    ImageEncoder <|-- MidnightEncoder
    _TimmEncoder <|-- UNI1Encoder
    _TimmEncoder <|-- UNI2Encoder
    _TimmEncoder <|-- H0miniEncoder
    _TimmEncoder <|-- H0Encoder
    _TimmEncoder <|-- H1Encoder
```

The contract every encoder fulfills consists of these members:

| Member | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `_build(weights_path)` | Abstract: constructs the backbone, resolves weights, returns `(model, transforms, hidden_dim)` |
| `forward(pixel_values)` | Pooled embedding used by the fallback MLP gene head |
| `forward_patch_tokens(pixel_values)` | Spatial tokens `(B, N, D)` consumed by the cross-attention decoder |
| `patch_dim` (property) | Per-patch embedding dimension, auto-detected from the underlying model |
| `hidden_dim` | Pooled output dimension, returned by `_build` |
| `NORM_MEAN` / `NORM_STD` | Encoder-specific normalization applied by its transforms |
| `LORA_TARGET_MODULES` | Names of attention submodules PEFT should target during fine-tuning |
| `set_transforms(**kwargs)` | Rebuilds the transform pipeline without reloading model weights |

Sources: [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L34-L105), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L108-L122)

> [!TIP]
> The `patch_dim` and `hidden_dim` split is deliberate: the cross-attention decoder sizes its queries with `patch_dim` (per-token, e.g. 1536 for Midnight), while the MLP fallback head sizes its input with `hidden_dim` (the pooled vector, e.g. 3072 for Midnight's concatenated CLS + mean-patch output). For encoders with compound pooling, these two values differ — swapping them silently misallocates decoder parameters.

## Supported Backbones

The module ships seven registered encoders spanning three weight-source families: Mahmood Lab pathology ViTs (UNI), Bioptimus pathology ViTs (H-optimus), a Kaiko AutoModel backbone (Midnight), and a CLIP vision tower. All operate on 224×224 tiles.

| Registry name | Backbone architecture | Upstream weights | `patch_dim` | `hidden_dim` | `forward()` pooling | Normalization |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `UNI1Encoder` | `vit_large_patch16_224` | MahmoodLab/UNI | 1024 | 1024 | CLS only | ImageNet |
| `UNI2Encoder` | `vit_giant_patch14_224` + SwiGLU + 8 register tokens | MahmoodLab/UNI2-h | 1536 | 1536 | CLS only | ImageNet |
| `H0miniEncoder` | `vit_base_patch14_reg4_dinov2` | bioptimus/H0-mini | 768 | 1536 (768×2) | CLS + mean patch | Bioptimus |
| `H0Encoder` | `vit_giant_patch14_reg4_dinov2` | bioptimus/H-optimus-0 | 1536 | 1536 | CLS only | Bioptimus |
| `H1Encoder` | `vit_giant_patch14_reg4_dinov2` | bioptimus/H-optimus-1 | 1536 | 1536 | CLS only | Bioptimus |
| `MidnightEncoder` | HF `AutoModel` (Kaiko ViT) | kaiko-ai/midnight | 1536 | 3072 (1536×2) | CLS + mean patch | 0.5 / 0.5 |
| `ImageCLIPEncoder` | CLIP vision tower + projection | local path only | 768 | 512 | Projected pooler | Read from processor |

Sources: [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L348-L356), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L156-L244), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L250-L343)

Normalization constants are module-level and shared by reference: `_IMAGENET_MEAN/_STD` for the UNI family, and `_BIOPTIMUS_MEAN/_STD` — the tissue-tuned statistics used by Bioptimus models — for the H-optimus family. This is why `NORM_MEAN`/`NORM_STD` live on the encoder class rather than in a global preprocessing config: mixing up a Bioptimus-normalized tile into a UNI encoder is the classic silent-degradation failure in pathology pipelines. `ImageCLIPEncoder` goes one step further and attempts to read mean/std from the checkpoint's bundled `AutoImageProcessor`, so fine-tuned CLIP variants with custom norms are handled automatically.

Sources: [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L154-L159), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L276-L286), [utils.py](src/deepspotm/utils.py#L6-L23)

## Pooling Strategies: CLS-Only vs CLS + Mean-Patch

`_TimmEncoder` implements two pooling modes selected by the `POOLING` class attribute. In `cls_only` mode (the default), `forward()` simply delegates to the timm model's classification-free head, returning the CLS embedding. In `cls_plus_mean_patch` mode, the encoder calls `forward_features`, strips prefix tokens using the model's `num_prefix_tokens`, and returns `cat(CLS, patch_tokens.mean(dim=1))` — doubling the output width, which is reflected in `HIDDEN_DIM`.

This is how two encoders on architecturally similar ViTs diverge in output shape: `H0miniEncoder` (ViT-Base, `embed_dim` 768) exposes `hidden_dim = 768 * 2 = 1536` because it concatenates, while `H0Encoder`/`H1Encoder` (ViT-Giant) stay at the raw 1536 CLS width. `MidnightEncoder` implements the same concatenation pattern directly in its own `forward`, bypassing the `_TimmEncoder` machinery since it is built from `transformers.AutoModel`.

Sources: [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L118-L151), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L202-L209), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L335-L339)

## Weight Resolution and the Offline-First Loading Contract

Weight lookup follows a deliberate precedence chain, implemented in two shared helpers. `_resolve_weights` prefers an explicit `weights_path` argument; failing that, it resolves the class's `HF_REPO_ID`/`HF_FILENAME` pair through `huggingface_hub.hf_hub_download` — critically, with `local_files_only=True`, so it only ever reads from the local HF cache and never initiates a network download. If neither source yields a file, it raises a `FileNotFoundError` with actionable guidance. `_load_state_dict` then auto-detects safetensors vs PyTorch `.bin` format and loads with `strict=True`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    B["Encoder construction"] --> W{"weights_path<br/>provided?"}
    W -->|Yes| L["Load local file<br/>(safetensors / .bin auto-detect)"]
    W -->|No| F{"_TimmEncoder<br/>subclass?"}
    F -->|Yes| C{"File present in<br/>local HF cache?"}
    C -->|Yes| L
    C -->|No| ERR["FileNotFoundError:<br/>'Download the model or pass weights_path'"]
    F -->|No| P{"pretrained flag?"}
    P -->|"True (Midnight)"| D["AutoModel.from_pretrained<br/>(may download)"]
    P -->|"False (Midnight)"| R["Random init from bundled<br/>midnight_config.json"]
    L --> T["Attach eval transforms<br/>(NORM_MEAN / NORM_STD)"]
    D --> T
    R --> T
```

The `pretrained=False` path is the key to the repository's offline-loading story. When set, `MidnightEncoder` builds the architecture from a bundled `midnight_config.json` with random initialization instead of touching the kaiko-ai/midnight repo — because the trained backbone weights are baked directly into DeepSpotM checkpoints and restored via `load_state_dict`. This is exactly the contract exercised by `DeepSpotM.from_pretrained`, which constructs the model with `backbone_pretrained=False` so that loading a published DeepSpotM model requires no network access to any upstream backbone repository. CLIP encoders are strict by contrast: `CLIPModel.from_pretrained(weights_path, local_files_only=True)` accepts only an explicit local path.

Sources: [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L6-L31), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L306-L333), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L251-L275)

> [!TIP]
> Tim encoders never hit the network — `_resolve_weights` uses `local_files_only=True`. If a `UNI1Encoder(...)` construction fails with `FileNotFoundError`, pre-download the weights via `huggingface_hub` (or pass `weights_path=` explicitly); the error message names the expected file. This offline-first design makes CI and air-gapped inference reproducible.

## Spatial Patch-Token Extraction

`forward_patch_tokens` is the bridge to the cross-attention decoder, and its base implementation is written to handle two model families generically rather than requiring every subclass to re-implement token surgery. For timm models, it calls `forward_features` to get the full token sequence and slices off `num_prefix_tokens` (CLS plus register tokens). For HuggingFace AutoModel outputs, it reads `last_hidden_state` and strips one CLS token (respecting `config.use_cls_token`) plus any `config.num_register_tokens` in the DINOv2 style. Anything outside these two families raises, forcing the subclass to provide an override.

Two concrete overrides exist. `ImageCLIPEncoder.forward_patch_tokens` slices `[:, 1:, :]` to drop the CLS token from the vision tower's hidden states. `MidnightEncoder.forward_patch_tokens` performs the same single-CLS strip. The practical consequence: register-token-equipped models (UNI2-h with 8, H0-mini/H-optimus with 4) return only true spatial patch positions, so the downstream decoder's `N_patches` is uniform across encoders of the same tile grid.

Sources: [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L70-L96), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L296-L298), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L341-L343)

## Factory API and Registry

Encoder selection is string-based. `ENCODER_REGISTRY` maps the seven class names to their implementations, and `build_encoder(name, **kwargs)` performs a validated lookup — raising a `ValueError` that lists available names on a miss. A companion function, `build_encoder_transforms(name, **kwargs)`, instantiates only the transform pipeline by reading the class-level `NORM_MEAN`/`NORM_STD` without constructing the model at all; this is useful for pre-processing tiles (e.g. in a WSI pipeline) on a machine where the backbone weights aren't present.

Sources: [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L346-L379)

## Integration Points with DeepSpotM

`DeepSpotM` wires the encoder in at four well-defined seams, visible in `model.py`:

1. **Construction** — `build_encoder(encoder_model, pretrained=backbone_pretrained)` builds the backbone; the constructor default is `encoder_model="MidnightEncoder"`. If `use_lora=True`, PEFT wraps the encoder using the encoder's own `LORA_TARGET_MODULES` — `"qkv"` for timm ViTs, `"q_proj"/"k_proj"/"v_proj"` for CLIP, `"query"/"key"/"value"` for Midnight. Otherwise the backbone is frozen outright. (The full save/load contract for wrapped models is covered in [LoRA Adaptation Contract](8-lora-adaptation-contract).)
2. **Decoder sizing** — the cross-attention gene decoder receives `patch_dim=self.backbone.patch_dim`, so changing the encoder automatically re-scales decoder projection layers.
3. **Forward dispatch** — cross-attention mode calls `backbone.forward_patch_tokens(pixel_values)`; MLP mode calls `backbone(pixel_values)` for the pooled vector.
4. **Transform mutation** — `set_eval_transforms` reaches through the PEFT wrapper chain (`PeftModel` → `LoraModel` → encoder) explicitly to invoke `set_transforms`, so predict-time options like `center_crop=True` work on LoRA-wrapped models.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as DeepSpotM.__init__
    participant F as build_encoder
    participant E as ImageEncoder
    participant P as PEFT (LoRA)
    U->>F: build_encoder("MidnightEncoder", pretrained=...)
    F->>E: MidnightEncoder(**kwargs)
    E->>E: _build() → (model, transforms, hidden_dim)
    E-->>F: encoder instance
    F-->>U: backbone
    U->>P: get_peft_model(backbone, LoraConfig(targets=backbone.LORA_TARGET_MODULES))
    U->>U: CrossAttentionGeneDecoder(patch_dim=backbone.patch_dim)
```

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L38-L95), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L97-L111), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L352-L365), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L378-L386), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L251-L254), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L301-L302)

## Extending the Encoder Zoo

Adding a new timm-based foundation model is declarative: subclass `_TimmEncoder`, set `TIMM_NAME` (plus `TIMM_KWARGS` if the architecture needs non-default timm arguments, as UNI2-h and H0-mini do with `SwiGLUPacked`/`SiLU`), point `HF_REPO_ID`/`HF_FILENAME` at the weights, declare `HIDDEN_DIM`, `NORM_MEAN`/`NORM_STD`, and optionally `POOLING`. If the model needs runtime-only timm imports, override `_build` to populate `TIMM_KWARGS` before delegating to `super()._build` — the pattern used to avoid importing timm at class-body evaluation time. For non-timm, non-standard-HF backbones, subclass `ImageEncoder` directly and override `_build`, `forward`, and `forward_patch_tokens`. Finally, register the class in `ENCODER_REGISTRY` so `build_encoder` can dispatch to it, and set `LORA_TARGET_MODULES` to match the new architecture's attention parameter names so LoRA fine-tuning binds correctly.

Sources: [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L172-L199), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L202-L224), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L346-L366)

## Where to Go Next

The encoder layer connects to several sibling topics in this catalog. To understand what happens to the patch tokens after extraction, continue to [Cross-Attention Gene Decoder](9-cross-attention-gene-decoder). For the details of PEFT wrapping, adapter targeting, and the state-dict prefix contract mentioned above, see [LoRA Adaptation Contract](8-lora-adaptation-contract). For the transform pipeline internals (`get_eval_transforms`, resizing, center-crop behavior), read [Image Preprocessing Transforms](18-image-preprocessing-transforms). For end-to-end loading of a published DeepSpotM checkpoint — which builds the backbone offline via the `pretrained=False` contract — see [Pretrained Model Loading](13-pretrained-model-loading) and [Memory-Efficient Source Loading](15-memory-efficient-source-loading). To see encoders exercised from the command line, start with [Command-Line Prediction Tools](3-command-line-prediction-tools).

# LoRA Adaptation Contract



This page explains the binding agreement between DeepSpotM's frozen pathology vision backbones, their LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adapters, and the checkpoint format that carries both. The "contract" is not a formal interface — it is a set of conventions about **wrapper topology, state-dict key prefixes, and trainability partitioning** that must hold simultaneously at training time and predict time. Break any one of them and loading fails silently or loudly, depending on which guard catches it first. This page documents the convention precisely so you can extend encoders, load checkpoints, or write custom inference code without violating it.

## Wrapper Topology: The Three-Layer Chain

DeepSpotM applies parameter-efficient fine-tuning through the HuggingFace **PEFT** library: `from peft import get_peft_model, LoraConfig` ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L6)). When `use_lora=True` (the default), the vision backbone produced by `build_encoder` is not used directly. Instead, `get_peft_model(self.backbone, lora_config)` wraps it, producing a fixed three-layer containment chain: `PeftModel` → `LoraModel` → `ImageEncoder` subclass. Attribute access to the original encoder must traverse `backbone.base_model.model` — and every state-dict key for backbone weights acquires the `backbone.base_model.model.` prefix ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L22-L36)).

The published DeepSpot-M model tokenizes H&E tiles with a **LoRA-adapted pathology foundation backbone (Midnight)** ([README.md](/README.md#L22-L32)), and the `DeepSpotM.__init__` default is `encoder_model="MidnightEncoder"` ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L40)). The wrapper chain looks like this:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    DS["DeepSpotM<br/>(pl.LightningModule)"] -->|".backbone"| PM["PeftModel<br/>(PEFT outer wrapper)"]
    PM -->|".base_model"| LM["LoraModel<br/>(PEFT adapter container)"]
    LM -->|".model"| ENC["ImageEncoder subclass<br/>e.g. MidnightEncoder"]
    ENC --> VIT["Vision Transformer blocks<br/>requires_grad = False"]
    ENC -.->|"adapters injected into<br/>query / key / value projections"| AD["LoRA A/B adapters<br/>requires_grad = True"]
    style AD fill:#e8f5e9
    style VIT fill:#f5f5f5
```

Sources: [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L6-L36), [image_encoder.py](/src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L34-L106), [README.md](/README.md#L22-L42)

## Adapter Injection Surface: `LoraConfig` Parameters

The LoRA configuration is constructed inline in `DeepSpotM.__init__` and exposes exactly one user-facing hyperparameter, the adapter rank `r` (default `8`, [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L54-L55)). Everything else is fixed by policy ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L86-L93)):

| Parameter | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `r` | `8` (hyperparameter) | LoRA rank — the only tunable knob, persisted via `save_hyperparameters` |
| `lora_alpha` | `r * 2` (i.e. `16` at default) | Scaling factor, locked at 2× rank |
| `lora_dropout` | `0.2` | Regularization on adapter activations |
| `target_modules` | `self.backbone.LORA_TARGET_MODULES` | Per-encoder injection points (see below) |
| Bias handling | PEFT default (`none`) | Frozen biases stay frozen |

Note that `target_modules` is read **from the encoder instance itself**, not hardcoded in `model.py`. This is the extensibility seam of the contract: each encoder family declares which leaf module names PEFT should instrument. The base `ImageEncoder` class defines the default `LORA_TARGET_MODULES = ["qkv"]`, matching fused query-key-value projections in timm ViT implementations ([image_encoder.py](/src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L36-L37)), and subclasses override it for their architecture's naming:

| Encoder | Architecture family | `LORA_TARGET_MODULES` | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UNI1Encoder`, `UNI2Encoder`, `H0Encoder`, `H0miniEncoder`, `H1Encoder` | timm ViT (fused `qkv`) | `["qkv"]` (inherited) | [image_encoder.py](/src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L162-L244) |
| `ImageCLIPEncoder` | HF CLIP vision (separate projections) | `["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"]` | [image_encoder.py](/src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L250-L254) |
| `MidnightEncoder` | HF AutoModel ViT (separate projections) | `["query", "key", "value"]` | [image_encoder.py](/src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L301-L304) |

The injected names are leaf-module attribute names resolved recursively by PEFT inside the wrapped encoder, so a new encoder subclass must either inherit the timm default or declare names matching its internal module tree. All seven encoders are registered in `ENCODER_REGISTRY` ([image_encoder.py](/src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L348-L366)) — for the full per-encoder normalization, pooling, and weight-resolution behavior, see [Pathology Vision Encoders](7-pathology-vision-encoders).

Sources: [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L54-L55), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L86-L93), [image_encoder.py](/src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L36-L37), [image_encoder.py](/src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L250-L254), [image_encoder.py](/src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L301-L304)

## Trainability Partitioning

LoRA establishes a strict split of learnable parameters, and the code relies on **who performs the freezing** as part of the contract. When `use_lora=True`, `model.py` deliberately does *not* freeze anything itself — the comment documents that "PEFT's `get_peft_model` freezes the underlying base model automatically and marks only the LoRA adapter parameters trainable" ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L81-L93)). When `use_lora=False`, the backbone is frozen explicitly via `freeze_backbone()` ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L94-L95), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L122-L124)), so either path yields a frozen vision backbone; LoRA simply swaps *which* few backbone-side parameters become trainable.

Consequently, a training run on a LoRA-wrapped model updates: (1) the LoRA A/B adapter matrices inside the backbone, and (2) the gene decoder (cross-attention, gene embeddings, optional router). The multi-billion-parameter foundation weights are never gradients-bearing. This is what allows the backbone's upstream weights — and later its adapted state — to travel together in one checkpoint.

Sources: [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L81-L95), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L122-L124)

## The Save/Load Contract: Prefixed-Key Symmetry

This is the core of the contract, stated verbatim in the `DeepSpotM` class docstring ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L22-L36)): **keep LoRA *wrapped* at predict time**. The state dict saved from training carries the `backbone.base_model.model.` prefix on frozen weights and sibling adapter keys beside them. The load path reconstructs the identical wrapper before any keys are matched:

1. `DeepSpotM.__init__` calls `save_hyperparameters(ignore=["kwargs"])` ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L70)), persisting `use_lora=True` and `r` into the checkpoint's `hyper_parameters`.
2. Every checkpoint-based constructor — Lightning's `load_from_checkpoint` (used by `DeepSpotM.load_for_inference` and `load_for_prediction` in [checkpoint.py](/src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L160-L163)) — instantiates `DeepSpotM(**hparams)`, which re-runs the `get_peft_model` wrap.
3. Only then does `load_state_dict` run, and the freshly created `backbone.base_model.model.*` keys line up with the checkpoint's.

> [!TIP]
> The symmetry is the point: because the prefix exists on *both* sides of the round-trip, no key remapping is ever needed. Calling `model.backbone.merge_and_unload()` in the inference path does not fail immediately — it silently breaks the *load-side* round-trip, because a freshly constructed `DeepSpotM(use_lora=True)` expects the prefixed keys and would report them all as unexpected ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L28-L36)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant T as Training
    participant C as Checkpoint
    participant L as Predict-time load
    T->>T: get_peft_model wraps encoder<br/>(frozen base + trainable adapters)
    T->>C: save: hparams (use_lora=True, r) +<br/>state_dict keys "backbone.base_model.model.*"
    L->>L: DeepSpotM(**hparams)<br/>re-wraps backbone via PEFT
    L->>C: load_state_dict(prefixed keys)
    C-->>L: adapters + frozen weights restored in place
    Note over L: merge_and_unload() here destroys<br/>prefix symmetry for future loads
```

The docstring enumerates the entry points that honor the contract: `forward` / `predict_genes` operate on the wrapped backbone, and `deepspotm.load_for_prediction` returns a wrapped model ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L27-L33)). Both public prediction paths call `self.backbone.forward_patch_tokens(pixel_values)` / `self.backbone(pixel_values)` directly ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L370-L391), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L406-L420)), relying on PEFT's `__getattr__` delegation to reach the inner encoder's methods — `examples/predict.py` calls the same wrapped methods without any unwrapping step ([predict.py](/examples/predict.py#L121-L125)).

Sources: [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L22-L36), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L70), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L370-L420), [checkpoint.py](/src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L89-L182), [predict.py](/examples/predict.py#L121-L125)

## Runtime Traversal Rules Through the Wrapper

Code that must reach *through* the PEFT wrappers follows two sanctioned patterns. The first is **implicit delegation**: PEFT forwards unknown attributes to the inner model, so `self.backbone.patch_dim` at construction time ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L98-L101)), `self.backbone.forward_patch_tokens(...)` in `forward` ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L379)), and `model.backbone.transforms` in the loaders ([checkpoint.py](/src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L180-L182), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L331)) all work without explicitly descending the chain.

The second pattern is **explicit traversal**, used where delegation failure would be silent. `set_eval_transforms` walks the chain by hand ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L352-L365)):

```python
for attr in ("base_model", "model"):
    if hasattr(backbone, attr) and not hasattr(backbone, "set_transforms"):
        backbone = getattr(backbone, attr)
backbone.set_transforms(**build_kwargs)
```

The comment explains the defensive posture: `__getattr__` delegation *usually* works, but the code is explicit "so a future PEFT release that breaks the chain won't silently regress to no-op" ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L358-L365)). When you write new code that must configure the inner encoder, follow the same rule of thumb: delegate for *reads* through well-tested attributes, but traverse explicitly when a silent failure would produce subtly wrong behavior (like predictions using train-time augmentation transforms instead of eval transforms).

Sources: [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L98-L101), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L352-L365), [checkpoint.py](/src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L180-L182)

## Published Artifact Side: Baked Adapters and LoRA-Tolerant Validation

The contract extends to the published Hugging Face artifact. `DeepSpotM.from_pretrained` expects `config.json` + `model.safetensors` + `tokens.csv`, and the safetensors file carries "vision backbone + LoRA adapters + gene decoder" baked in ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L251-L275)). This is why loading sets `hparams["backbone_pretrained"] = False`: the Midnight backbone is built offline from a bundled config with random init, then overwritten wholesale by the checkpoint — no network access to the upstream `kaiko-ai/midnight` repo is needed ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L267-L270), [image_encoder.py](/src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L306-L315)).

The validation logic in `from_pretrained` is the LoRA-aware half of the contract ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L303-L316)). It loads with `strict=False`, then inspects the `missing` keys with a namespace-aware filter: only keys starting with the substantive namespaces (`gene_decoder.`, `backbone.`) **and not containing "lora"** are treated as errors.

> [!TIP]
> The `"lora" not in k.lower()` clause exists because a clean safetensors export may omit PEFT bookkeeping buffers while keeping all adapter weights. The filter tolerates that benign absence while still raising a `RuntimeError` if genuinely substantive weights (frozen backbone or decoder) are missing — meaning "config and weights disagree." The same philosophy of explicit drift-surfacing governs `check_state_dict_load` in [checkpoint.py](/src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L57-L86).

Sources: [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L251-L331), [image_encoder.py](/src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L306-L315), [checkpoint.py](/src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L57-L86)

## Contract Violation Modes

The following table summarizes what happens when each clause of the contract is broken — most failures are *silent*, which is precisely why the contract is documented rather than left as tribal knowledge:

| Violation | Consequence | Detected by |
|---|---|---|
| `merge_and_unload()` before save/inference reuse | Prefixed keys no longer match; downstream `load_state_dict` treats everything as unexpected | Silent breakage of round-trip; surfaces only at next load ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L28-L36)) |
| Overriding `LORA_TARGET_MODULES` with names absent from the module tree | PEFT injects no adapters; backbone trains nothing | Silent — no training of backbone-side parameters |
| Stripping `backbone.base_model.model.` prefixes from a checkpoint | All backbone keys become unexpected at load | Silent with `strict=False`; drift guards catch unfiltered paths ([checkpoint.py](/src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L57-L86)) |
| Constructing `DeepSpotM(use_lora=False)` for a LoRA checkpoint | Key sets structurally incompatible | Key drift at `load_state_dict` |
| Relying on PEFT delegation for *stateful* configuration | Future PEFT change silently no-ops | Only if you follow the explicit-traversal pattern ([model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L358-L365)) |

## Where to Go Next

The contract sits between two neighbors in the component stack. Upstream, [Pathology Vision Encoders](7-pathology-vision-encoders) details the encoders whose `LORA_TARGET_MODULES` declarations you saw here, and [Architecture Overview](6-architecture-overview) places the adapted backbone within the full model. Downstream, the checkpoint machinery that enforces the load-side guarantees is covered in [Pretrained Model Loading](13-pretrained-model-loading) and [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling); the loading path that rebuilds the wrapper from persisted hyperparameters is [Memory-Efficient Source Loading](15-memory-efficient-source-loading). To see the wrapped model consumed end-to-end, continue to the [TCGA-SKCM Tutorial Notebook](4-tcga-skcm-tutorial-notebook).

# Cross-Attention Gene Decoder



The Cross-Attention Gene Decoder is DeepSpotM's gene prediction head: it takes frozen pathology patch tokens from the vision backbone and, through stacked cross-attention blocks, lets one *query per gene* read out morphology-relevant evidence and project it into a predicted expression value. This page explains the decoder's two implementation levels — the reusable `CrossAttentionLayer` primitive and the composite `CrossAttentionGeneDecoder` — including its forward data flow, the three-element output contract, output-head selection, interpretability path, and in-place vocabulary retargeting. Details of the pluggable query sources and output heads are covered by their dedicated pages: [Gene Router Hypernetwork](10-gene-router-hypernetwork) and [Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings).

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L34-L38), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L98-L118)

## Architectural Role: From Patch Tokens to Gene Expression

Within `DeepSpotM`, the decoder sits at the end of the pipeline: the vision backbone (wrapped by LoRA — see [LoRA Adaptation Contract](8-lora-adaptation-contract)) exposes `forward_patch_tokens(pixel_values)`, and the model's `forward` passes those tokens straight into `self.gene_decoder`, returning the decoder's triple `(expression, pooled, attn_weights)` unchanged to the caller. When `use_cross_attention` is disabled (an ablation toggle), the entire decoder is replaced by a plain MLP head over pooled backbone features — which clarifies what the cross-attention path adds: per-gene, token-level readout instead of a single pooled-vector regression.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L370-L391), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L107-L118)

The decoder performs three transformations: project patch tokens into the query space (K/V), refine gene queries against those keys/values via cross-attention, and map each refined query to a scalar expression value. Everything is built to operate in one shared width `D` (`gene_embed_dim`), so attention, layer norms, and the output head all live in the same dimensional space.

| Tensor | Shape | Producer | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `patch_tokens` | `(B, N, patch_dim)` | backbone `forward_patch_tokens` | decoder input |
| `patch_kv` | `(B, N, D)` | `patch_proj` (Linear) | attention keys/values |
| gene queries | `(B, G, D)` | query slot (embedding or adapter) | one row per gene |
| refined queries | `(B, G, D)` | stacked `CrossAttentionLayer`s | morphology-conditioned gene state |
| `expression` | `(B, G)` | output head | prediction |
| `gene_features` | `(B, D)` | mean-pool over G | aggregated slide representation |
| `attn_weights` | `list[(B, H, G, N)]` or `None` | attention layers | only when `need_weights=True` |

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L713-L731), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L787-L791)

## The CrossAttentionLayer Primitive

Each decoder layer is a standard **pre-norm cross-attention block**: multi-head attention where the *queries* are gene embeddings and the *keys/values* are patch tokens, followed by a residual + `LayerNorm`, then a 4×-expansion feed-forward network (`Linear(D→4D)` → GELU → dropout → `Linear(4D→D)`) with a second residual + norm. Two details matter for downstream consumers: `batch_first=True` so tensors arrive as `(B, seq, D)`, and `average_attn_weights=False` so per-head attention survives into the return value — the foundation of the interpretability path.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L38-L62)

Because the patch keys/values `patch_kv` are computed once by `patch_proj` and reused by every layer, stacking layers (default: 2 in the shipped configuration) lets each gene query progressively narrow which patches it attends to, while the compute cost stays linear in layer count.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L528-L534), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L44-L48)

## Composite Anatomy: CrossAttentionGeneDecoder

To read the composite class, it helps to see it as **three pluggable slots plus a fixed attention spine**: (1) a patch projection into attention space, (2) a gene-query source that produces `(G, D)` query templates, and (3) an output head that collapses each query to a scalar. The constructor wires these slots differently depending on `init_gene_embeddings`, with an early `return` cleanly separating the multi-source branch from the single-source branch.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L474-L602)

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class DeepSpotM {
        +gene_decoder: CrossAttentionGeneDecoder
        +forward(pixel_values, gene_indices)
        +predict_genes(pixel_values, genes)
        +get_gene_attention_maps(pixel_values, gene_indices)
        +swap_gene_vocabulary(...)
    }
    class CrossAttentionGeneDecoder {
        +patch_proj: Linear(patch_dim, D)
        +layers: ModuleList~CrossAttentionLayer~
        +gene_embeddings / multi_source
        +output_proj OR router / routers
        +swap_vocabulary(bio_emb)
        +forward(patch_tokens, gene_indices)
    }
    class CrossAttentionLayer {
        +cross_attn: MultiheadAttention
        +norm1 norm2: LayerNorm
        +ffn: Linear(D,4D)-GELU-Linear(4D,D)
    }
    class MultiSourceGeneEmbedding {
        +adapters: ModuleDict
        +modality_emb: frozen buffer
        +set_active(name)
    }
    class GeneRouter {
        +weight_net: per-gene projection MLP
        +bias_net: per-gene bias MLP
    }
    DeepSpotM *-- CrossAttentionGeneDecoder : owns
    CrossAttentionGeneDecoder *-- CrossAttentionLayer : num_layers x
    CrossAttentionGeneDecoder o-- MultiSourceGeneEmbedding : query slot, multi-source
    CrossAttentionGeneDecoder o-- GeneRouter : output head, optional
```

The query source and output head are chosen independently but with one coupling: the router mode **requires** a biological embedding — `use_router=True` with `init_gene_embeddings="xavier"` raises a `ValueError`, because per-gene generated projections can only be derived from a real gene prior. The three construction modes are:

| Mode | `init_gene_embeddings` | Query source | Output head options |
|---|---|---|---|
| Random | `"xavier"` | `nn.Embedding(n_genes, D)`, xavier-uniform | shared `Linear(D, 1)` only |
| Single-source | one registry name (e.g. `"scgpt"`) | `nn.Embedding(n_genes, bio_dim)` initialized from the prior + bias-free `gene_query_proj` when `bio_dim ≠ D` | shared head **or** one `GeneRouter` reading a frozen bio buffer |
| Multi-source | list of names (e.g. `["evo2", "orthrus", …]`) | `MultiSourceGeneEmbedding`: per-source trainable bio parameter + adapter (+ optional frozen one-hot modality vector) | shared head **or** one `GeneRouter` **per source** (`routers: ModuleDict`) |

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L528-L602), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L108-L150)

In multi-source mode, per-source routers deliberately read `multi_source.current_bio` — the same trainable bio parameter that feeds the active adapter — preserving the single-source design invariant that "the same biological embedding feeds adapter (query init) and router (output hypernet)," now per dispatchable source. The embedding-source mechanics and modality encoding are documented in [Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings).

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L559-L583)

## Forward Data Flow

Prerequisite for the flowchart: the decoder's `forward` accepts `(patch_tokens, need_weights, gene_bio_embeddings, gene_indices)`. `patch_tokens` are `(B, N, patch_dim)`; `gene_indices` is an optional 1-D `LongTensor` that may arrive as a plain list (it is converted via `torch.as_tensor` and moved to the input device); `gene_bio_embeddings` is a zero-shot override available only on the single-source router path.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L713-L736)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S["forward(patch_tokens, gene_indices)"] --> P["patch_proj → patch_kv (B, N, D)"]
    P --> Q{"multi_source configured?"}
    Q -->|"yes"| MS["active source adapter projects bio → queries<br/>(G_sel, D), then expand → (B, G_sel, D)"]
    Q -->|"no"| SS{"gene_indices given?"}
    SS -->|"yes"| GI["gene_embeddings[indices] → (G_sel, bio_dim)"]
    SS -->|"no"| ALL["gene_embeddings[0..G) → (G, bio_dim)"]
    GI --> PRJ["gene_query_proj (only if bio_dim ≠ D)"]
    ALL --> PRJ
    MS --> ATT["stacked CrossAttentionLayers<br/>queries attend to patch_kv"]
    PRJ --> ATT
    ATT --> HEAD{"use_router?"}
    HEAD -->|"yes"| R["router(bio_emb_subset, queries) → (B, G_sel)"]
    HEAD -->|"no"| LIN["output_proj(queries).squeeze(-1) → (B, G_sel)"]
    R --> OUT["(expression, gene_features, attn or None)"]
    LIN --> OUT
```

Both query branches converge on the same attention spine: queries are expanded to the batch dimension (`unsqueeze(0).expand(B, -1, -1)` — no memory copy), run through `num_layers` cross-attention blocks, and only then hit the output head. When `gene_indices` is provided, **only the selected gene queries are ever built and attended**, so compute scales with `len(gene_indices)` rather than the full panel — the property that powers [Selective Gene Prediction](16-selective-gene-prediction) end to end.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L738-L758), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L370-L391)

> [!TIP]
> In multi-source mode, the adapter projection happens **before** the batch expansion: the `Linear(bio_dim_i → D)` runs on `(G, bio_dim_i)` rather than `(B, G, bio_dim_i)`, reducing projection cost from `B·G·bio_dim·D` to `G·bio_dim·D`. The code comments this explicitly as the reason the multi-source path orders projection-then-expand, unlike the naive single-source ordering.

> [!TIP]
> On the multi-source router path, the decoder passes `multi_source.current_bio.detach()` into the router. The detach is load-bearing gradient routing, not an optimization: it ensures the trainable bio parameters receive gradients **only** through the adapter (query) pathway. Without it, bio would be co-optimized simultaneously by the adapter, `router.weight_net`, and `router.bias_net` — dynamics the authors note previously degraded validation Pearson correlation.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L422-L424), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L762-L777)

## The Output Contract: A Verified Three-Tuple

`forward` always returns `(expression, gene_features, attn_weights)` — a triple that downstream integrations unpack positionally. The contract tests state this explicitly: a tiny randomly-initialized decoder is constructed in CI precisely so the tuple's shapes and semantics can be asserted without downloading the gated checkpoint, and the test module's docstring records that **TIAToolbox unpacks exactly this three-tuple**, making the signature a compatibility surface, not an internal detail.

Sources: [tests/test_decoder.py](tests/test_decoder.py#L1-L8), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L787-L791)

| Element | Shape | Semantics | Default behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expression` | `(B, G_sel)` | predicted expression; columns follow `gene_indices` order when subsetting | full panel `G` when no indices |
| `gene_features` | `(B, D)` | mean of refined gene queries over the G axis | always computed |
| `attn_weights` | `list[(B, H, G, N)]` per layer, or `None` | per-head attention maps | `None` unless `need_weights=True` |

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L787-L791), [tests/test_decoder.py](tests/test_decoder.py#L46-L54)

Two behaviors of `gene_indices` are pinned by dedicated tests. First, subsetting is *exact*: `decoder(patch_tokens, gene_indices=wanted)` returns columns identical (within float tolerance) to `full[:, wanted]` — proving that selecting indices computes the same values as slicing the full output, while skipping work for unselected genes. Second, **request order is output order**: reversing the requested index tensor reverses the output columns, so callers can request genes in any arbitrary order (e.g. matching an external panel's column layout) without post-hoc reordering.

Sources: [tests/test_decoder.py](tests/test_decoder.py#L57-L65), [tests/test_decoder.py](tests/test_decoder.py#L68-L77)

## Output Heads: Shared Projection vs. Gene Router

With `use_router=False`, the head is a single shared `nn.Linear(D, 1)` applied to every refined query — one weight vector for all genes. With `use_router=True` (the shipped default is enabled at the `DeepSpotM` level), each gene's projection vector and bias scalar are *generated on the fly* from its biological embedding via the router's two MLPs and applied with `einsum('bgd,gd->bg')`. This is what enables zero-shot prediction: the decoder's forward accepts a `gene_bio_embeddings` override on the single-source path, letting callers pass embeddings for genes **outside the trained vocabulary** — the shared head fundamentally cannot do this.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L713-L729), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L760-L787), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L50-L52)

| Aspect | Shared `output_proj` | `GeneRouter` hypernetwork |
|---|---|---|
| Per-gene weights | one shared `Linear(D, 1)` | generated per gene from its bio embedding |
| Unseen genes | unsupported | supported via `gene_bio_embeddings` override |
| Construction requirement | any query init | requires a biological embedding source (not `"xavier"`) |
| Multi-source variant | single shared head | one router per source, dispatched on `active_source` |

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L559-L583), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L107-L150)

The router is documented in full on [Gene Router Hypernetwork](10-gene-router-hypernetwork); for this page the essential point is that the decoder treats it as a swappable head slot, and the dispatch logic in `forward` (multi-source `routers[active]` vs single-source `router`) is entirely internal to the decoder.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L760-L787)

## Interpretability: Per-Gene Attention Over Patches

Requesting `need_weights=True` changes the return's third slot from `None` to a list of per-layer, per-head attention tensors of shape `(B, H, G, N)` — preserved intact because every `CrossAttentionLayer` sets `average_attn_weights=False`. The model-level helper `get_gene_attention_maps` builds on this: it temporarily forces eval mode, collects all layers' weights, takes the **last layer's** tensor and averages over heads to produce `(B, G, N_patches)` — each gene's spatial attention footprint over the input patches — optionally sliced by `gene_indices`. The method refuses to run when `use_cross_attention=False`, since the MLP fallback produces no attention.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L52-L62), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L425-L454)

## In-Place Vocabulary Retargeting via `swap_vocabulary`

The decoder can be retargeted to a different gene panel **without reconstruction**: `swap_vocabulary(bio_emb, ...)` replaces the query embeddings and reconfigures the head, with surgical rules for what is rebuilt versus preserved. The guiding principle, stated in the code, is to *preserve trained weights whenever shapes still fit* — e.g. swapping human ProtT5 for mouse ProtT5 (both 1024-d) keeps the trained `gene_query_proj` and router verbatim, changing only the embedding table's contents. The `gene_embed_dim` property (derived from `patch_proj.out_features`) is what lets the swap logic infer `D` without storing it redundantly.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L604-L614), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L656-L678)

| Component | Condition | Action on swap |
|---|---|---|
| `gene_embeddings` | always | rebuilt from the new `(n_genes_new, bio_dim_new)` tensor |
| `gene_query_proj` | `bio_dim_new == D` | set to `None` (passthrough) |
| `gene_query_proj` | `bio_dim_new` unchanged ≠ D | **kept** — trained projection preserved |
| `gene_query_proj` | `bio_dim_new` differs | rebuilt as bias-free `Linear` |
| `router` / `_router_bio_emb` | input dim matches | bio buffer updated; router weights **kept** |
| `router` | input dim differs, or switching on | rebuilt (`router_hidden_dim` inherited from the old router when unset) |
| head/router cross-switch | `use_router` flipped | the stale head (`output_proj` or router) is deleted cleanly |
| multi-source mode | `source` argument required | collapses to that source via `collapse_to_source`; other sources' routers dropped; `use_router`/`router_hidden_dim` arguments ignored |

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L639-L711)

The model-level wrapper `DeepSpotM.swap_gene_vocabulary` adds validation (embedding row count must match the token CSV's gene list, otherwise `ValueError`) and keeps `hparams` consistent so a subsequent checkpoint save/load round-trips the swapped configuration. Checkpoint-side handling of vocabulary changes is covered in [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling).

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L124-L190)

## Configuration Reference

The decoder's architecture is fully exposed as `DeepSpotM` hyperparameters ("every component can be toggled on/off for ablation studies," per the class docstring), which are persisted into checkpoints and replayed on load.

| Hyperparameter | Default | Effect on the decoder |
|---|---|---|
| `use_cross_attention` | `True` | selects this decoder over the pooled-MLP fallback |
| `gene_embed_dim` | 256 | shared width `D` for patch projection, queries, attention, and head |
| `cross_attn_heads` | 8 | attention heads per layer |
| `cross_attn_layers` | 2 | number of stacked `CrossAttentionLayer`s |
| `cross_attn_dropout` | 0.1 | dropout in attention and the FFN |
| `init_gene_embeddings` | `"xavier"` | query-init mode: `"xavier"` / source name / list of names |
| `use_router` | `True` | hypernetwork head instead of shared `Linear(D, 1)` |
| `router_hidden_dim` | `None` → `2·D` | hidden width inside the router MLPs |
| `use_modality_encoding` | `True` | adds the frozen one-hot modality vector to queries (multi-source only) |
| `bio_dims` | `None` | per-source bio dims for checkpoint-driven reconstruction (skips `.pt` assets) |

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L43-L52), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L98-L118), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L546-L557)

Note the checkpoint-reconstruction subtlety: when `bio_dims` is provided (the `from_pretrained` path), the multi-source branch allocates zero-filled bio parameters by shape and lets `load_state_dict` overwrite them, so loading a published model never needs to open the raw gene-embedding asset files.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L546-L557), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L300-L310)

## Where to Go Next

The decoder's query slot and output head are each deep enough to warrant their own treatment: continue with [Gene Router Hypernetwork](10-gene-router-hypernetwork) for the zero-shot output-head mathematics, and [Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings) for adapter and modality-encoding internals. To see `gene_indices` applied end-to-end at inference time — including the `predict_genes` convenience wrapper that maps gene symbols to indices and returns only the requested columns — read [Selective Gene Prediction](16-selective-gene-prediction); for the vocabulary side that defines `n_genes` and the gene→index mapping the decoder relies on, see [Gene Vocabulary and Output Mapping](12-gene-vocabulary-and-output-mapping).


# Gene Router Hypernetwork



This page explains the **GeneRouter** — the hypernetwork that serves as the output head of DeepSpot-M's cross-attention gene decoder. A hypernetwork is a network whose weights *produce* the weights of another network; here, two small MLPs read a gene's biological embedding (scGPT, Evo 2, Orthrus, ProtT5, Apertus, …) and generate that gene's projection vector and bias on the fly, instead of storing a fixed per-gene weight matrix. This design is what allows one checkpoint to predict expression for genes it never saw during training — the repository's stated zero-shot capability.

Scope of this page: module anatomy, the construction matrix (single-source vs. multi-source), runtime dispatch and gradient behavior, vocabulary-swap semantics, and the unseen-gene pathways. It sits between [Cross-Attention Gene Decoder](9-cross-attention-gene-decoder) (query refinement) and [Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings) (query initialization).

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L23-L41), [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L110-L145)

## Architectural Role: One Shared Head vs. Generated Per-Gene Heads

Without the router, the decoder's output head is a single shared projection — `nn.Linear(gene_embed_dim, 1)` — meaning every gene's refined query vector is squeezed through the *same* scalar projection. The router replaces this: for gene *g* with biological embedding *bio_g*, it computes a dedicated projection `w_g = weight_net(bio_g)` and bias `b_g = bias_net(bio_g)`, then produces the prediction as an inner product between the gene's refined query and its generated weight, plus the generated bias. The biological embedding effectively acts as a *content address* into a space of output projections, so a gene that never appeared in training can still receive a meaningful projection as long as a biological embedding for it exists.

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L578-L589), [README.md](/README.md#L35-L41)

The following data-flow diagram shows where the router sits relative to the decoder's query pathway — the biological embedding feeds **both** the query initialization (via the embedding/projection path) and the output head (via the router MLPs), which is the design invariant the code repeatedly preserves ("same embedding feeds adapter + router"):

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    PATCH["patch_tokens (B, N, patch_dim)"] -->|"patch_proj"| KV["patch_kv (B, N, D)"]
    BIO["_router_bio_emb (G, bio_dim)<br/>frozen buffer / per-source bio param"] --> Q0["gene query embeddings<br/>gene_query_proj → (B, G, D)"]
    Q0 --> CA["CrossAttentionLayer × num_layers"]
    KV --> CA
    CA --> QN["refined gene_queries (B, G, D)"]
    BIO -->|"router.weight_net → (G, D)"| EIN
    BIO -->|"router.bias_net → (G,)"| EIN["einsum('bgd,gd-&gt;bg') + bias"]
    QN --> EIN
    EIN --> OUT["expression (B, G)"]
```

| Property | Shared head (`output_proj`) | GeneRouter |
|---|---|---|
| Output weights | One `Linear(D, 1)`, shared by all genes | Per-gene `(D,)` projection, generated per forward from `bio_g` |
| New/unseen gene | Impossible — no weight exists for it | Works — MLP evaluates on any bio embedding of matching dim |
| Parameter count | `D + 1` | Two MLPs, **independent of the number of genes** G |
| Biological prior usage | Query init only | Query init **and** output head |

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L110-L145), [README.md](/README.md#L23-L31)

## Module Anatomy: Two MLPs and an Einstein Sum

`GeneRouter` is deliberately minimal — two independent `nn.Sequential` MLPs and no internal state. `weight_net` maps `(G, bio_dim) → (G, D)` through a `Linear → GELU → Linear` stack (input `gene_bio_dim`, hidden `hidden_dim`, output `gene_embed_dim`); `bias_net` shares the same hidden width but outputs a scalar per gene, squeezed to `(G,)`. The default hidden size is `gene_embed_dim * 2` when `router_hidden_dim` is not supplied.

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L119-L133)

The forward pass is a single expression: `torch.einsum('bgd,gd->bg', gene_queries, proj) + bias`. Because `proj` and `bias` depend only on gene identity — not on the image — they are computed **once per gene**, independent of batch size. For a batch of B tiles the cost is `G × bio_dim × H + G × H × D` for generation plus one batched bilinear product; the biological embeddings are shared across the batch dimension, which is what makes this head cheap relative to re-attending per gene.

| Stage | Operator | Input → Output shape |
|---|---|---|
| Projection generation | `weight_net(bio)` | `(G, bio_dim)` → `(G, D)` |
| Bias generation | `bias_net(bio).squeeze(-1)` | `(G, bio_dim)` → `(G,)` |
| Score computation | `einsum('bgd,gd->bg')` | `(B, G, D)`, `(G, D)` → `(B, G)` |
| Output | `+ bias` | `(B, G)` |

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L135-L145)

## Construction Matrix: When Is a Router Built?

Router construction is decided by the interaction of two decoder arguments: `init_gene_embeddings` (which biological prior, if any) and `use_router`. The decoder validates their combination at construction time — a router with no biological input is a logical contradiction and raises `ValueError`. At the `DeepSpotM` level, `use_router` defaults to `True` and is forwarded into the decoder alongside `router_hidden_dim`.

| `init_gene_embeddings` | `use_router=False` | `use_router=True` |
|---|---|---|
| `"xavier"` (random init) | Shared head, standard path | **`ValueError`** — no biological embedding to condition on |
| Single source name (e.g. `"scgpt"`) | Shared head; bio initializes queries only | Registers `_router_bio_emb` **buffer** (frozen prior) + `self.router = GeneRouter(bio_dim, D, hidden)` |
| List of sources (multi-source) | Shared head + `MultiSourceGeneEmbedding` queries | `self.routers = nn.ModuleDict(...)` — one `GeneRouter` **per source**, each built with that source's own `bio_dim` |

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L498-L512), [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L545-L563), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L48-L50), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L97-L111)

The per-source construction preserves the single-source invariant under multi-source dispatch: each `GeneRouter` receives `gene_bio_dim=self.multi_source.bio_dims[name]`, so a 1280-d text prior and a 512-d RNA prior each get a router whose input layer matches their embedding width. In the no-router multi-source branch, the decoder falls back to the shared `Linear(gene_embed_dim, 1)` head and returns early, skipping the single-source initialization entirely.

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L545-L563)

## Multi-Source Dispatch and the Gradient Contract

At runtime the decoder never iterates routers — it dispatches to exactly one: `self.routers[active]`, where `active` is `self.multi_source.active_source`, selected externally via `DeepSpotM.set_source`. The biological input is obtained through the `current_bio` property, which returns the **trainable** `bio_{source}` parameter for the active source — with one critical modification: it is passed as `current_bio.detach()`.

> [!TIP]
> The `.detach()` is a deliberate gradient-routing decision, documented inline: the router *reads* the bio embedding's current value but backpropagation does **not** flow into `bio_{source}` through the router pathway. Bio parameters receive gradients only via the adapter (query) path. Without this isolation, a single bio tensor would be co-optimized by three consumers simultaneously — the adapter, `weight_net`, and `bias_net` — a dynamic the authors report as unstable enough to hurt validation Pearson correlation.

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L760-L777), [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L391-L408), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L196-L211)

This makes the two modes gradient-equivalent at the router boundary: the single-source `_router_bio_emb` is a frozen *buffer* (never trained at all), while the multi-source `bio_*` are trainable *parameters* that train only through the adapter path. The concept relationship below summarizes which consumers write gradients back into the biological embedding:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    BIO["bio_&lt;source&gt; Parameter<br/>(G, bio_dim)"]
    BIO -->|"forward + gradient"| AD["adapter (Linear + LayerNorm)<br/>→ gene queries"]
    BIO -.->|"forward only — detached"| RN["routers[active].weight_net"]
    BIO -.->|"forward only — detached"| RB["routers[active].bias_net"]
    AD --> CA["cross-attention refinement"]
    CA --> OUT["expression (B, G)"]
    RN --> OUT
    RB --> OUT
```

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L763-L777), [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L386-L408)

Because `active_source` is a plain Python attribute — intentionally excluded from `state_dict` — a freshly loaded multi-source checkpoint has no active pathway until `set_source` is called; the loader-side contract for this is covered in [Pretrained Model Loading](13-pretrained-model-loading) and [Memory-Efficient Source Loading](15-memory-efficient-source-loading).

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L175-L181), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L196-L211)

## Runtime Flow Through `forward`

The full forward sequence through the decoder, with the router as the final stage:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant M as DeepSpotM
    participant D as CrossAttentionGeneDecoder
    participant MS as MultiSourceGeneEmbedding
    participant R as routers[active_source]
    M->>D: forward(patch_tokens, gene_indices)
    D->>MS: forward(gene_indices) — adapter + modality encoding
    MS-->>D: queries (G_sel, D), expanded to (B, G_sel, D)
    D->>D: CrossAttentionLayer refinement
    D->>MS: current_bio.detach(), indexed by gene_indices
    D->>R: forward(router_bio, gene_queries)
    R-->>D: einsum('bgd,gd->bg') + bias → (B, G_sel)
    D-->>M: (expression, gene_features, attn_weights)
```

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L713-L790), [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L370-L391)

Subsetting interacts correctly with the router because the biological input is indexed with the *same* `gene_indices` used to gather queries (`router_bio = router_bio[gene_indices]`), preserving column alignment. The repository's contract tests pin the surrounding guarantee the router relies on: `gene_indices` must both **subset** the output and **respect requested order** (`subset ≡ full[:, wanted]`, and reversed indices flip output columns accordingly).

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L774-L784), [test_decoder.py](/tests/test_decoder.py#L57-L77)

## Vocabulary Surgery: `swap_vocabulary` Router Semantics

When a checkpoint is retargeted to a new gene vocabulary (custom panel, cross-species), the decoder's `swap_vocabulary` applies conservative rebuild rules to the router — trained router weights are preserved whenever mathematically possible:

| Scenario | Router action |
|---|---|
| New vocab, **same** `bio_dim` (e.g. human prott5 → mouse prott5, both 1024-d) | Keep the trained router verbatim; refresh the `_router_bio_emb` buffer to the new vocab's embeddings |
| New vocab with **different** `bio_dim`, or no router yet | Rebuild `GeneRouter(bio_dim_new, D, hidden)`; inherit hidden width from the old router |
| Explicit `use_router=False` | Create shared head; delete `router` and the `_router_bio_emb` buffer |
| Multi-source + `source=` | Collapse to one source; kept source's router preserved, all other routers deleted (`use_router`/`router_hidden_dim` ignored) |

> [!TIP]
> The hidden-width inheritance trick: `swap_vocabulary` reads the trained hidden dim by introspection — `existing_router.weight_net[0].out_features` — rather than trusting a passed argument. This means a same-dim vocabulary swap round-trips with zero architectural drift, and an explicit `router_hidden_dim` only takes effect when a rebuild is genuinely required.

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L608-L712), [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L684-L698)

The model-level wrapper `DeepSpotM.swap_gene_vocabulary` exposes this surgery and keeps `hparams["use_router"]` (and the multi-source collapse reflected in `init_gene_embeddings`) synchronized so that a subsequent `load_from_checkpoint` rebuilds the identical structure — the checkpoint round-trip aspect is detailed in [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling).

Sources: [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L126-L191)

## Zero-Shot and Unseen-Gene Pathways

The router enables unseen-gene prediction through two mechanisms at different abstraction levels. At the **decoder level**, `CrossAttentionGeneDecoder.forward` accepts an optional `gene_bio_embeddings` override of shape `(G, bio_dim)` which bypasses the stored buffer entirely — the documented hook for zero-shot inference on arbitrary genes. Its hard constraint is dimensional: `bio_dim` must match the router's trained input width (`weight_net`'s first layer), since the hypernetwork's weights were learned for a specific embedding geometry. Note that the public `DeepSpotM.forward` does not surface this argument; the override lives at the decoder API boundary.

Sources: [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L713-L729), [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L778-L785)

At the **model level**, retargeting to a genuinely new vocabulary goes through `swap_gene_vocabulary` (embeddings + token CSV in, rebuilt router out), which is the path used by fine-tuning and cross-vocabulary workflows. When reconstructing a multi-source model from a checkpoint alone, the `bio_dims` hyperparameter drives shape-only construction (`MultiSourceGeneEmbedding.from_shapes`) so per-source routers can be allocated without downloading raw embedding assets — the trained values then arrive via `load_state_dict`.

Sources: [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L126-L191), [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L529-L538)

## Configuration Reference

| Parameter | Defined in | Default | Effect on the router |
|---|---|---|---|
| `use_router` | `DeepSpotM.__init__` → decoder | `True` | Selects hypernetwork head over shared `Linear(D, 1)` |
| `router_hidden_dim` | `DeepSpotM.__init__` → router | `None` → `gene_embed_dim * 2` | Hidden width of both router MLPs; recovered by introspection on vocab swaps |
| `init_gene_embeddings` | `DeepSpotM.__init__` → decoder | `"xavier"` | Source of bio embeddings; must be non-xavier for the router; a list builds per-source routers |
| `gene_embed_dim` | `DeepSpotM.__init__` → decoder | `256` | Router output width; must match the decoder's query space |
| `use_modality_encoding` | decoder → `MultiSourceGeneEmbedding` | `True` | Adjacent concern — affects queries, not router weights |

Sources: [model.py](/src/deepspotm/model.py#L38-L67), [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L119-L133), [modules.py](/src/deepspotm/modules.py#L498-L512)

## Summary and Next Steps

The Gene Router Hypernetwork is a small component with outsized consequences: two MLPs turn a gene's frozen biological identity into a bespoke output projection, making the model's output space *queryable* rather than fixed. Its implementation is characterized by three verified invariants — construction-time validation that a router always has a biological input, per-source router dispatch with detached bio reads in multi-source mode, and conservative weight preservation across vocabulary surgery.

To continue through this section of the catalog: [Cross-Attention Gene Decoder](9-cross-attention-gene-decoder) covers the query refinement stage feeding the router, [Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings) covers the `bio_*` parameters and adapters it consumes, and [Gene Vocabulary and Output Mapping](12-gene-vocabulary-and-output-mapping) covers how the router's output columns map back to gene symbols. For inference-time engineering around these components, see [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling) and [Selective Gene Prediction](16-selective-gene-prediction).


# Multi-Source Gene Embeddings



This page explains the machinery that lets a single DeepSpotM decoder draw gene identity from *several* independent biological embedding spaces — DNA, RNA, protein, single-cell, and text foundation models — and switch between them at runtime. The centerpiece is `MultiSourceGeneEmbedding`, a per-source stack of trainable gene-token parameters, projection adapters, and a frozen modality signal, orchestrated by a runtime `active_source` selector. It sits between the [Cross-Attention Gene Decoder](9-cross-attention-gene-decoder), which consumes the queries it produces, and the [Gene Router Hypernetwork](10-gene-router-hypernetwork), which shares the same per-source embeddings for output projections.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L148-L181), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L47-L66)

## Why Multiple Biological Priors

DeepSpot-M's gene decoder does not treat genes as fixed output columns; each gene is a queryable embedding that attends to image patch tokens. The multi-source design generalizes this: instead of committing to one prior (e.g. scGPT alone), the model ships one gene-embedding bank per source — the five published sources are `evo2`, `orthrus`, `prott5`, `scgpt`, and `apertus` — plus one trainable adapter and, in router mode, one hypernetwork per source. The shared cross-attention stack is identical to the single-source path; only the gene-query generation and the output head become per-source and runtime-dispatched. This is what lets `from_pretrained(..., source="scgpt")` and `--source evo2` select a pathway on the same published weights.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L24-L42), [examples/predict.py](examples/predict.py#L16-L16), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L213-L236)

The dispatch is **exclusive, not fused**: exactly one source is active per forward pass. There is no concatenation or averaging of sources — the invariant maintained throughout is *"the same embedding feeds the adapter (query init) and the router (output hypernet)"*, extended on a per-source basis. Switching sources therefore changes the model's complete gene-identity pathway, which is why the selection must be made explicitly before every forward.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L547-L561), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L391-L399)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph REG["_GENE_EMB_LOADERS registry"]
        L1["evo2 .pt"]
        L2["orthrus .pt"]
        L3["scgpt .pt"]
        L4["prott5 / apertus .pt"]
    end
    subgraph MS["MultiSourceGeneEmbedding"]
```
