```mermaid
        B1["bio_evo2 Parameter"]
        B2["bio_orthrus Parameter"]
        B3["bio_scgpt Parameter"]
        A1["adapter: Linear + LayerNorm"]
        A2["adapter: Linear + LayerNorm"]
        A3["adapter: Linear + LayerNorm"]
        M["modality_emb buffer<br/>frozen one-hot"]
        S["active_source selector"]
    end
    subgraph DEC["CrossAttentionGeneDecoder"]
        CA["shared cross-attention layers"]
        R["routers ModuleDict<br/>one GeneRouter per source"]
    end
    L1 --> B1 --> A1
    L2 --> B2 --> A2
    L3 --> B3 --> A3
    S --> MS
    A1 --> Q["gene queries G x D"]
    A2 --> Q
    A3 --> Q
    M --> Q
    Q --> CA --> R
    B1 -.->|current_bio.detach| R
    B2 -.->|current_bio.detach| R
    B3 -.->|current_bio.detach| R
```

## The Source Registry and the Asset Contract

Every source is registered in `_GENE_EMB_LOADERS` as a `partial` bound to a `<name>_gene_embeddings.pt` file inside the packaged `deepspotm.assets` directory. Loading goes through `_load_gene_embeddings`, which uses `importlib.resources` (so the assets resolve from an installed wheel, not just a source checkout) and `weights_only=True` for safe deserialization. A missing asset raises a `FileNotFoundError` that points to the generating notebooks rather than failing opaquely. To add a new source, you must register both its loader and — if modality encoding is enabled — its modality mapping.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L458-L470), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L95-L104), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L77-L78)

| Registry key | Asset file | Modality (`MODALITY_BY_SOURCE`) | Published default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `evo2` | `evo2_7b_gene_embeddings.pt` | `dna` | ✅ |
| `orthrus` | `orthrus_gene_embeddings.pt` | `rna` | ✅ |
| `prott5` | `prott5_gene_embeddings.pt` | `protein` | ✅ |
| `esm2` | `esm2_gene_embeddings.pt` | `protein` | — |
| `scgpt` | `scgpt_gene_embeddings.pt` | `single_cell` | ✅ |
| `geneformer` | `geneformer_gene_embeddings.pt` | `single_cell` | — |
| `geneformer_cancer` | `geneformer_cancer_gene_embeddings.pt` | `single_cell` | — |
| `string_network` | `string_network_gene_embeddings.pt` | *(unmapped)* | — |
| `apertus` | `apertus_gene_embeddings.pt` | `text` | ✅ |
| `genept_ada` | `genept_ada_gene_embeddings.pt` | `text` | — |
| `genept_m3` | `genept_m3_gene_embeddings.pt` | `text` | — |

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L79-L92), [examples/predict.py](examples/predict.py#L16-L16)

Note that `string_network` is loadable but intentionally absent from `MODALITY_BY_SOURCE` — sources without a modality entry can only be used with `use_modality_encoding=False`. All sources in one multi-source model must also share the same gene count; the constructor rejects mismatched first dimensions, since each bank is row-aligned with the same ordered vocabulary from `tokens.csv`.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L90-L92), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L203-L209), [config.py](src/deepspotm/config.py#L11-L16)

## Modality Encoding: Frozen Categorical Signals

When `use_modality_encoding=True` (the default for multi-source models), each gene query gains an explicit signal about *which modality* of prior produced it. The vocabulary `("dna", "rna", "protein", "single_cell", "text")` has a canonical, load-bearing ordering — the index is what the one-hot encoding reads, so new modalities must be **appended** to keep existing checkpoints valid. The encoding itself is a `(n_modalities, gene_embed_dim)` buffer with an identity on the first *n* columns; it is registered as a buffer rather than a parameter deliberately: modality identity is categorical, there is nothing for the model to *learn* about it — only how to *use* it via cross-attention.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L65-L71), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L246-L280)

Two consequences are worth internalizing. First, modality is keyed by *modality*, not source name: `evo2` and a future `hyenaDNA` would both map to `dna` and share the same token, letting cross-attention exploit modality-level invariances. Second, the design imposes structural constraints enforced at construction: `gene_embed_dim` must be ≥ 5 to fit the one-hot into the query space, and every registered source must appear in `MODALITY_BY_SOURCE` or construction raises a `ValueError` suggesting registration or ablation via `use_modality_encoding=False`. A consistency test pins both the vocabulary subset relation and the ordering.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L73-L78), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L255-L268), [tests/test_decoder.py](tests/test_decoder.py#L89-L94)

## Anatomy of `MultiSourceGeneEmbedding`

Each source gets two kinds of learned state plus one bookkeeping attribute. The **gene-token bank** is a trainable `nn.Parameter` named `bio_{source}` of shape `(n_genes, bio_dim_i)`, initialized *directly from the raw biological prior with no rescaling* — mirroring the single-source `nn.Embedding` copy path and deliberately preserving per-gene learnable degrees of freedom. Cross-source scale differences are handled not by normalization but by trusting AdamW's per-element second-moment estimates. The **adapter** is a `Linear(bio_dim_i, gene_embed_dim) → LayerNorm` pair; the trailing LayerNorm normalizes per gene, so the shared cross-attention sees comparably-scaled queries regardless of which source's dimensional space they came from.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L148-L181), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L216-L234)

The dispatch state, `active_source`, is a *plain Python attribute — deliberately excluded from both parameters and buffers* so it never enters the `state_dict`. This is the module's central contract, and it has a hard corollary: after any checkpoint load, `active_source` is `None`, and both `forward()` and the `current_bio` property raise `RuntimeError` until a source is selected.

> [!TIP]
> The exclusion of `active_source` from the state dict is why "freshly loaded checkpoint → forward" always fails. Every loader that returns a model (`from_pretrained`, `load_for_inference`) calls `set_source` internally; any custom loading path you write must do the same before the first forward pass.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L242-L244), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L404-L409), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L430-L434)

### Two construction paths

The class offers two classmethods corresponding to the two lifecycle stages of a model:

| | `from_registry` | `from_shapes` |
|---|---|---|
| Input | list of source *names* | `{name: bio_dim}` mapping (`bio_dims`) |
| Bank initialization | loads each `.pt` prior from packaged assets | zeros of the given shape |
| Intended for | fresh training-time builds | checkpoint loading (`from_pretrained`) |
| Opens asset files | yes, one per source | no — shapes only |
| Validation | row count vs `n_genes`, unknown-name rejection | adapter input shapes checked by strict `state_dict` load |

The zero-initialized `from_shapes` route exists because a published checkpoint already carries the trained `bio_{source}` tensors: the raw `.pt` priors are unnecessary, and skipping them means loading needs no access to the embedding assets at all. `bio_dims` itself is derived metadata, not persisted state — the adapters' input shapes carry the same information.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L282-L324), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L214-L215), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L59-L66)

## Runtime Dispatch: The `set_source` Contract

At the model level, dispatch is exposed as `DeepSpotM.set_source(name)`, which validates against the decoder's `MultiSourceGeneEmbedding` and delegates to `set_active`. Read-side symmetry is provided by the `sources` property (registered names, or `None` for single-source models) and `current_source` (the active name, or `None` for single-source or freshly loaded multi-source checkpoints). The published CLI mirrors this: `predict.py` exposes `--source` with `choices=["evo2", "orthrus", "prott5", "scgpt", "apertus"]` and defaults to `scgpt`.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L196-L211), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L333-L350), [examples/predict.py](examples/predict.py#L62-L65), [examples/predict.py](examples/predict.py#L161-L162)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant M as DeepSpotM
    participant MS as MultiSourceGeneEmbedding
    participant D as CrossAttentionGeneDecoder
    participant R as routers[active]
    C->>M: set_source("orthrus")
    M->>MS: set_active("orthrus")
    Note over MS: active_source = "orthrus"<br/>plain attribute, NOT in state_dict
    C->>M: forward(pixel_values, gene_indices=None)
    M->>D: forward(patch_tokens)
    D->>MS: forward(gene_indices)
    MS->>MS: adapters["orthrus"](bio_orthrus)
    MS->>MS: queries += modality_emb[idx("rna")]
    MS-->>D: (G, gene_embed_dim)
    D->>D: expand to (B, G, D), cross-attend to patches
    D->>R: router(current_bio.detach(), gene_queries)
    R-->>C: expression (B, G)
```

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L193-L211), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L411-L442), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L738-L742)

## Forward Pass Mechanics: Efficient Projection and Gradient Routing

`MultiSourceGeneEmbedding.forward` returns a `(G, gene_embed_dim)` query template — the decoder performs the batch expansion. When `gene_indices` is supplied for [Selective Gene Prediction](16-selective-gene-prediction), the bank is *indexed before the adapter*, so the projection cost is `G · bio_dim · D` instead of the `B · G · bio_dim · D` a post-expand projection would incur. After the adapter, the active source's frozen modality vector is broadcast-added to every query, and the decoder expands to `(B, G, D)` symmetrically with the single-source path.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L411-L442), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L738-L742)

The output head in multi-source + router mode is an `nn.ModuleDict` of per-source `GeneRouter`s, each sized to its own `bio_dim`. The routing step reads the active bank via `current_bio` — but with a decisive twist: it is **detached** first.

> [!TIP]
> `router_bio = current_bio.detach()` mirrors the single-source design, where the router reads a frozen `_router_bio_emb` buffer. Without the detach, `bio_{source}` would be co-optimized by three simultaneous consumers — the adapter, `router.weight_net`, and `router.bias_net` — producing unstable training dynamics that measurably hurt validation Pearson. Gradient reaches the banks exclusively through the adapter pathway; the router sees the banks' current values but never shapes them.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L761-L777), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L547-L561)

In non-router multi-source mode, a single shared `output_proj` head is used instead, and the routers are not built at all. The `use_router` decision is therefore orthogonal to multi-source capability, but only the router mode consumes the per-source bank a second time.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L562-L564), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L786-L787)

## Collapse: Specialization and Memory-Efficient Deployment

Because only one source is ever active, the other banks are dead weight at inference. Two mechanisms exploit this. `collapse_to_source(name, new_bio_emb)` prunes the module in place: it deletes every other source's `bio_` parameter and adapter, re-registers the kept source's bank (re-registration, not `.data.copy_`, because `n_genes` *may change* — the documented cross-species case grows orthrus from ~20k human genes to 74,815 mouse genes at a constant 512-d), prunes the modality index mapping, and sets `active_source` to the survivor. The kept adapter and the surrounding decoder's per-source router retain their trained weights verbatim, since `bio_dim` must match.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L333-L385)

At the model level this is surfaced by `swap_gene_vocabulary(..., source=...)`, which additionally prunes the other sources' routers and — critically for persistence — rewrites `hparams["init_gene_embeddings"]` to `[source]`, so a subsequently saved checkpoint round-trips as a naturally single-source model. Inference-side, `load_for_inference(path, source=...)` never collapses at all: it overrides `init_gene_embeddings` to `[source]` so the module is *built* with only one bank and adapter (opening just one `.pt` via the registry), loads with `strict=False` so the other sources' tensors in the checkpoint are silently dropped, then calls `set_source`. Passing `source=` to a genuinely single-source checkpoint is surfaced as an explicit `RuntimeError` rather than silently losing the `bio_emb` weights under `strict=False`.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L126-L191), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L213-L249), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L639-L655)

The published multi-source checkpoint holds all five banks and adapters — roughly **750 MB** on disk — so `from_pretrained` also requires an explicit `source=` whenever more than one source is present, and `from_pretrained` reads `bio_dims` from the repo's `config.json` to drive the shape-only build. These deployment workflows are covered in depth on [Memory-Efficient Source Loading](15-memory-efficient-source-loading) and [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling).

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L217-L229), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L294-L305), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L318-L327)

## Single-Source vs Multi-Source: Pattern Summary

| Aspect | Single-source path | Multi-source path |
|---|---|---|
| `init_gene_embeddings` | `"xavier"` or one source name | list/tuple of source names |
| Gene query state | `nn.Embedding` + optional `gene_query_proj` | per-source `bio_{name}` Parameter + `Linear+LayerNorm` adapter |
| Router input | frozen `_router_bio_emb` buffer | `current_bio.detach()` (trainable, adapter-fed) |
| Output head | one `GeneRouter` or shared `output_proj` | `nn.ModuleDict` of routers or shared `output_proj` |
| Modality encoding | ignored | optional frozen one-hot added to queries |
| Selection step | none | `set_source()` before *every* forward |
| Vocabulary swap | `swap_vocabulary(bio_emb)` in place | requires `source=` → `collapse_to_source` |
| Checkpoint build | reads one `.pt` at init | `bio_dims` shape-only build, zero asset access |

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L522-L564), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L566-L602)

For debugging, `extra_repr` renders the full dispatch state — source names, per-source `bio_dims`, the source→modality mapping (or `"disabled"`), and the current `active_source` — making a mis-set selector visible in any `print(module)`.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L444-L455)

## Where to Go Next

The natural continuations of this page: [Gene Router Hypernetwork](10-gene-router-hypernetwork) details the `weight_net`/`bias_net` MLPs consuming `current_bio.detach()`; [Gene Vocabulary and Output Mapping](12-gene-vocabulary-and-output-mapping) explains the `tokens.csv` alignment every bank depends on; [Pretrained Model Loading](13-pretrained-model-loading) covers the `from_pretrained` + `source=` contract; [Memory-Efficient Source Loading](15-memory-efficient-source-loading) expands on `load_for_inference`; and [Selective Gene Prediction](16-selective-gene-prediction) shows how `gene_indices` interacts with the pre-adapter indexing described above.


# Gene Vocabulary and Output Mapping



When DeepSpotM predicts gene expression from a histology tile, the raw output of `forward()` is just a tensor of shape `(B, G)` — a grid of numbers with no biological meaning attached. What turns column 42 into "KCnj6" and not "BRCA1" is a **vocabulary contract**: an ordered list of gene symbols, shipped inside the package, that binds every output column to exactly one gene. This page explains how that vocabulary is stored, how it becomes the model's output order, how predictions map back to gene names, and how a model can be retargeted to a different vocabulary. It is the bridge between the decoder architecture you saw in [Cross-Attention Gene Decoder](9-cross-attention-gene-decoder) and the inference utilities described in [Pretrained Model Loading](13-pretrained-model-loading) and [Selective Gene Prediction](16-selective-gene-prediction).

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L370-L391), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L11-L32)

## The Vocabulary File: tokens.csv

The single source of truth is a bundled CSV asset, `tokens.csv`, resolved at import time by `config.py` through `importlib.resources` (with a filesystem fallback for source-tree runs). Resolving the path this way — rather than hard-coding a relative path — is what guarantees the vocabulary works when the package is installed as a wheel, a property the test suite explicitly verifies.

The file contains more than genes. Each row has three columns — `token`, `token_type`, and `token_id` — and three token categories coexist:

| token_type | Count | token_id range | Role in the output contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gene` | 19,338 | 0 – 19337 | **The output vocabulary** — defines prediction column order |
| `disease` | 15 | 19338 – 19352 | Ancillary tokens; excluded from prediction |
| `tissue` | 13 | 19353 – 19365 | Ancillary tokens; excluded from prediction |
| `special` | 2 (`<PAD>`, `<MASK>`) | 19366 – 19367 | Bookkeeping tokens; excluded from prediction |

Sources: [config.py](src/deepspotm/config.py#L8-L17), [tokens.csv](src/deepspotm/assets/tokens.csv#L1-L15), [tokens.csv](src/deepspotm/assets/tokens.csv#L19336-L19370), [test_structure_expression.py](tests/test_structure_expression.py#L8-L19)

The critical invariant is **ordering**: gene rows appear first, in sorted position, and their `token_id` matches their row order. The first genes are `NAALADL1` (id 0), `REXO2` (id 1), `KCNJ6` (id 2), and the last gene before the disease block is `HAPLN1` (id 19337). This positional layout means "gene index" and "row order in the CSV" are the same thing — the foundation every downstream mapping relies on.

Sources: [tokens.csv](src/deepspotm/assets/tokens.csv#L1-L15), [tokens.csv](src/deepspotm/assets/tokens.csv#L19336-L19360)

## From CSV to Canonical Gene Order

Three pieces of code cooperate to turn the CSV into the model's vocabulary state, and each has a distinct responsibility:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["tokens.csv<br/>(token, token_type, token_id)"] -->|"pd.read_csv +<br/>filter token_type=='gene'"| B["StructureExpression<br/>gene_names_ordered"]
    B -->|"gene_names / n_genes /<br/>_gene_to_idx"| C["DeepSpotM<br/>vocabulary state"]
    C -->|"n_genes"| D["CrossAttentionGeneDecoder<br/>gene_embeddings rows"]
    D -->|"output column i"| E["prediction tensor (B, G)<br/>column i == gene_names[i]"]
    C -.->|"genes_to_indices()"| D
```

**Step 1 — Parsing.** `StructureExpression` reads the CSV (from an explicit `token_path` if given, otherwise the packaged default) and filters to `token_type == 'gene'` with pandas. The result, `gene_names_ordered`, is the canonical gene ordering. The same class also serves the *training-side* reverse mapping: `structure_expression()` converts a `{gene: value}` dict into a fixed-length tensor aligned to that ordering, zero-filling unmeasured genes, clamping negatives, and producing a boolean mask — unknown symbols are silently ignored so they cannot shift a value into the wrong column.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L11-L32), [test_structure_expression.py](tests/test_structure_expression.py#L21-L33)

**Step 2 — Model state.** `DeepSpotM.__init__` instantiates `StructureExpression` and copies the ordering into three attributes that define the output contract:

| Attribute | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `gene_names` | `list[str]` | The public, ordered gene panel — **output column `i` of `forward()` corresponds to `gene_names[i]`** |
| `n_genes` | `int` | Vocabulary size (19,338 by default); sizes every vocab-dependent layer |
| `_gene_to_idx` | `dict[str, int]` | Reverse lookup, symbol → column index, used for selective prediction |

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L71-L81), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L97-L117)

**Step 3 — Decoder sizing.** The cross-attention decoder receives `n_genes` and allocates one gene query embedding per vocabulary row (`nn.Embedding(n_genes, bio_dim)` in the single-source path, or per-source bio parameters in the multi-source path). Because queries are built by iterating over vocabulary indices, the decoder's output is vocabulary-ordered by construction.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L97-L117), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L592-L603), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L744-L752)

> [!TIP]
> The vocabulary also travels with published checkpoints: `DeepSpotM.from_pretrained` downloads/reads `tokens.csv` alongside `config.json` and `model.safetensors`, then injects it as `token_path`. A checkpoint and its vocabulary are therefore always loadable as one consistent unit — never mix a checkpoint's weights with a different `tokens.csv`.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L251-L331)

## The Output Mapping Contract

For a full-panel prediction, the contract is simple and positional:

- `forward(pixel_values)` returns `expression` of shape `(B, n_genes)`;
- `expression[b, i]` is the predicted expression of `gene_names[i]` for tile `b`;
- when the decoder uses the router output head, the per-gene projection weights are likewise indexed by the same vocabulary positions, so routing does not reorder anything.

The decoder achieves this by building gene queries for `arange(n_genes)` when no subset is requested — literally walking the vocabulary in order — then cross-attending each query against the patch tokens and projecting to a scalar. If you disable the cross-attention decoder entirely (the MLP `gene_head` fallback), the same contract holds: the final `nn.Linear` emits exactly `n_genes` columns in vocabulary order.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L370-L391), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L713-L752), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L760-L790), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L112-L117)

## Selective Prediction: When Column Order Follows the Caller

Asking for a subset of genes introduces a second ordering rule, and confusing the two is the most common beginner mistake. The selective path works as follows:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User code
    participant M as DeepSpotM
    participant D as GeneDecoder
    U->>M: predict_genes(img, ["PTPRC", "EPCAM", "CD3D"])
    M->>M: genes_to_indices(genes) → [i_PTPRC, i_EPCAM, i_CD3D]
    M->>D: forward(patch_tokens, gene_indices=idx)
    D->>D: build queries ONLY for the selected rows
    D->>D: cross-attend selected queries (compute ∝ len(genes))
    D->>D: router bio vectors subselected by the same indices
    D-->>M: expression (B, 3)
    M-->>U: columns in USER's order: PTPRC, EPCAM, CD3D
```

Two methods implement the symbol→index translation and the subsetting:

| API | Input | Output | Output column order |
|---|---|---|---|
| `forward(pixel_values)` | image tensor | `(B, n_genes)` | **Vocabulary order** (`gene_names`) |
| `forward(pixel_values, gene_indices=idx)` | image + index tensor | `(B, len(idx))` | **`idx` order** |
| `genes_to_indices(["EPCAM", "CD3D"])` | symbol(s) | `LongTensor` of indices | caller's symbol order |
| `predict_genes(img, genes)` | image + symbol(s) | `(B, len(genes))` | **caller's symbol order** |
| `get_gene_attention_maps(img, gene_indices)` | image + optional indices | `(B, G_sel, N_patches)` | vocabulary order (or `gene_indices` order) |

Unknown symbols are not silently skipped: `genes_to_indices` raises a `KeyError` listing the offending names (truncated to the first ten), so a typo like `EPCAMM` fails loudly at the call site. Beyond convenience, the subset path is also a compute optimization — the decoder builds and cross-attends only the requested queries, so cost scales with `len(genes)` rather than 19,338. The deeper mechanics of that optimization are covered in [Selective Gene Prediction](16-selective-gene-prediction).

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L370-L391), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L393-L404), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L406-L420), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L713-L790), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L425-L453)

> [!TIP]
> `predict_genes` returns columns in **your** order, not the vocabulary's — pass `["CD3D", "EPCAM"]` and you get those columns back in exactly that sequence. Only full-panel `forward()` output is guaranteed vocabulary-ordered, so always zip against the list you passed in (or `model.gene_names`), never against a hardcoded assumption.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L406-L420)

## Mapping Predictions Back to Gene Names in Practice

The bundled CLI example, `examples/predict.py`, shows the end-to-end mapping workflow and is the best template for your own inference code. It chooses the column labels first — `list(genes)` when scoring specific genes, otherwise `list(model.gene_names)` — then keeps prediction rows and label columns aligned through batching, ranking, and export:

- **Top-k report**: for full-panel predictions, it zips `gene_names` with each row's values and sorts by predicted value to print the highest-expression genes per tile with their symbols.
- **Targeted scoring**: with `--genes EPCAM CD3D PTPRC`, it delegates to `predict_genes` and prints `symbol=value` pairs in the order given; a `KeyError` from the vocabulary lookup is caught and reported as "unknown gene symbol(s)".
- **CSV export**: `--output preds.csv` writes a DataFrame whose *columns are gene names* and rows are tiles — the mapping contract made tangible in a file you can open in pandas.

Sources: [predict.py](examples/predict.py#L127-L165), [predict.py](examples/predict.py#L167-L209)

For interpretability, the same contract extends to attention: `get_gene_attention_maps` returns per-gene attention over spatial patches shaped `(B, G_selected, N_patches)`, with rows indexed in vocabulary order (or `gene_indices` order when subsetting), so `attn[b, i]` describes where the model "looked" for `gene_names[i]`.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L425-L453)

## Retargeting to a Different Vocabulary

A trained model is not permanently bound to its 19,338-gene panel. `DeepSpotM.swap_gene_vocabulary(embeddings_path, token_path, ...)` rebuilds every vocabulary-dependent layer in place so a checkpoint can be pointed at a custom panel (e.g. a mouse vocabulary or a small marker set) before loading vocab-specific weights. The model-side wrapper performs the bookkeeping — refresh `n_genes`, update hyperparameters so checkpoints round-trip — while validation happens against the new token file:

| Validation / bookkeeping step | What happens |
|---|---|
| Token list load | Parses the new `token_path`, filtering `token_type == 'gene'` — same rule as the default vocabulary |
| Shape check | The `.pt` embedding tensor's row count must equal the new gene list length, or a `ValueError` is raised naming both counts |
| Decoder rebuild | `swap_vocabulary` replaces `gene_embeddings`, rebuilds `gene_query_proj` only when the embedding dimension changes, and rebuilds or swaps the router/shared output head — preserving trained weights wherever shapes allow |
| Model state update | `n_genes` refreshed; router overrides and multi-source collapses recorded in `hparams` for checkpoint round-trips |

Two details matter when you do this. First, the method requires the cross-attention decoder — a checkpoint built with the MLP `gene_head` has no vocabulary-specific layers to swap, and the method raises `RuntimeError` if you try. Second, on multi-source models you must pass `source=` to name which embedding pathway survives the swap; the model collapses to that single source and the others' parameters are dropped. The checkpoint-side story — how the new vocabulary's weights are then loaded consistently — is covered in [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling).

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L127-L191), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L608-L711)

## Where the Vocabulary Does *Not* Apply

A few adjacent concepts look vocabulary-related but follow separate rules, and this page deliberately stops at their boundary. The **modality vocabulary** (`dna`, `rna`, `protein`, `single_cell`, `text`) is a frozen one-hot encoding over embedding *sources*, not genes — reordering it would invalidate existing checkpoints, which is why the source code marks it "DON'T reorder" — and the gene-embedding **source registry** (`scgpt`, `prott5`, `evo2`, …) controls which biological prior initializes queries and routers, not which genes are predicted. Both are documented in [Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings) and [Gene Router Hypernetwork](10-gene-router-hypernetwork). Likewise, the runtime selection of an active source via `set_source` is a *dispatch* decision orthogonal to gene-column mapping, and it is deliberately not persisted in the state dict — see [Memory-Efficient Source Loading](15-memory-efficient-source-loading).

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L65-L92), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L458-L470), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L333-L350)

## Summary and Next Steps

The gene vocabulary is a single ordered CSV (`tokens.csv`, 19,338 gene rows) whose row positions *are* the model's output columns. `StructureExpression` extracts that ordering, `DeepSpotM` exposes it as `gene_names`/`n_genes`/`_gene_to_idx`, and the decoder produces columns in exactly that order for full-panel predictions. Subsetting via `predict_genes` reorders columns to the caller's symbol list while shrinking compute proportionally. Retargeting to a new panel is a validated, in-place swap that rebuilds only the shape-dependent layers.

Suggested reading from here:

- Going deeper on architecture: [Cross-Attention Gene Decoder](9-cross-attention-gene-decoder) explains what those gene queries attend to; [Gene Router Hypernetwork](10-gene-router-hypernetwork) covers the per-gene output head referenced above.
- Inference engineering: [Selective Gene Prediction](16-selective-gene-prediction) expands on the subset-compute path; [Pretrained Model Loading](13-pretrained-model-loading) and [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling) cover how vocabularies and weights travel together.
- Hands-on: [Command-Line Prediction Tools](3-command-line-prediction-tools) walks through `predict.py` end to end, and the [TCGA-SKCM Tutorial Notebook](4-tcga-skcm-tutorial-notebook) shows the mapping workflow in a runnable notebook.


# Pretrained Model Loading



DeepSpotM ships pretrained weights in two artifact formats, and this page documents the exact contract for turning either into a ready-to-use `(model, image_processor)` pair. You will learn the three public loading entry points, the file layout each expects, the state-dict integrity guards that prevent silent uninitialised-weight inference, and the two invariants that most often surprise new users: LoRA keys must stay PEFT-prefixed, and gene-source selection is *not* stored in the state dict.

## Loading Entry Points at a Glance

The library exposes three loaders, each tuned to a different artifact and resource profile. All of them converge on the same terminal state: model on the requested device, in `eval()` mode, with center-crop evaluation transforms installed on the backbone. [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L272-L274), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L98-L99)

| Entry point | Artifact | Weights format | Multi-source handling | Typical caller |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DeepSpotM.from_pretrained()` | HF repo or local directory (`config.json` + `model.safetensors` + `tokens.csv`) | safetensors | `source=` arg selects/collapses the pathway | Default for published releases; used by `examples/predict.py` |
| `deepspotm.load_for_prediction()` | Raw Lightning `.ckpt` | PyTorch state dict | Auto-infers single source; requires `source=` otherwise; optional cross-vocab swap | Training-repo checkpoints |
| `DeepSpotM.load_for_inference()` | Raw Lightning `.ckpt` | PyTorch state dict | Builds *only* the named source's bank/adapter | Memory-constrained multi-source inference |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Checkpoint artifact"] --> B{"Which format?"}
    B -->|"config.json + model.safetensors + tokens.csv"| C["DeepSpotM.from_pretrained()"]
    B -->|"Raw Lightning .ckpt"| D["deepspotm.load_for_prediction()"]
    C --> E{"Multi-source?"}
    E -->|"1 source"| F["auto-select source"]
    E -->|">1 sources + source= given"| G["collapse to named source"]
    E -->|">1 sources, no source"| ERR["ValueError"]
    D --> H{"token_path + gene_embeddings_path?"}
    H -->|"no"| I["Lightning load_from_checkpoint"]
    I --> J{"model.sources?"}
    J -->|"None"| K["eval prep"]
    J -->|"1 source"| L["infer + set_source"]
    J -->|">1 + source= given"| M["set_source"]
    J -->|">1, no source"| ERR2["ValueError"]
    F --> K
    G --> K
    L --> K
    M --> K
    K --> N["model.to(device).eval()<br/>set_eval_transforms(center_crop=True)"]
    N --> O["Return (model, image_processor)"]
```

The decision logic above is verified in the loader implementations: source inference rules for `from_pretrained` at [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L318-L327) and for `load_for_prediction` at [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L169-L178). Note that cross-vocabulary loading (the `token_path` branch) is documented in depth on [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling) — this page covers only its placement in the dispatch flow.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L251-L331), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L89-L183), [predict.py](examples/predict.py#L156-L162)

## Loading a Published Release with `from_pretrained`

`DeepSpotM.from_pretrained(repo_id_or_path)` is the canonical way to consume a published model. It accepts either a Hugging Face repo id (e.g. `"ratschlab/DeepSpotM"`, optionally pinned with `revision=`) or a local directory, and downloads — or reads — exactly three files:

| File | Role | Consumption detail |
|---|---|---|
| `config.json` | Saved hyper-parameters, including `bio_dims` | JSON-loaded into `hparams`; the `_deepspotm_format_version` marker is popped before construction |
| `model.safetensors` | Baked-in weights: vision backbone + LoRA adapters + gene decoder | Loaded via `safetensors.torch.load_file`, applied with `load_state_dict(strict=False)` |
| `tokens.csv` | The gene vocabulary | Passed as `token_path` so the constructor resolves the ordered gene list |

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L263-L298), [config.py](src/deepspotm/config.py#L11-L16)

Two construction-time overrides make this path self-contained and network-light. First, the loader forces `backbone_pretrained=False`, so the vision backbone's architecture is built *without* downloading upstream weights — they arrive from the safetensors file instead, meaning no network access to the upstream backbone repository is needed at load time. Second, `bio_dims` from `config.json` lets the gene decoder allocate per-source parameters purely by shape, without reading the raw gene-embedding `.pt` assets. Both flags exist solely for checkpoint loading; their defaults preserve training-time behaviour. [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L57-L67)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph ART["Release artifacts"]
        CFG["config.json"]
        WTS["model.safetensors"]
        TOK["tokens.csv"]
    end
    CFG --> HP["hparams<br/>token_path ← tokens.csv<br/>backbone_pretrained ← False"]
    HP --> BB["build_encoder(pretrained=False)"]
    BB --> PEFT["get_peft_model →<br/>LoRA-wrapped backbone"]
    HP --> DEC["CrossAttentionGeneDecoder<br/>(allocated via bio_dims)"]
    TOK --> DEC
    WTS --> LOAD["load_state_dict(strict=False)"]
    LOAD --> GUARD["drift filter:<br/>only gene_decoder./backbone.<br/>namespaces, lora keys exempt"]
    GUARD --> SEL["set_source()"]
    DEC --> SEL
    SEL --> DONE["model.to(device).eval()<br/>center-crop transforms"]
```

Because the export format may omit PEFT bookkeeping buffers, `from_pretrained` does not naively reject every missing key. Instead it runs a *targeted* drift check: only keys under the substantive namespaces `gene_decoder.` or `backbone.` are inspected, and any key whose name contains `lora` (case-insensitive) is exempt. Unexplained drift in real weights raises a `RuntimeError` that names the first offending keys and states that "the config and weights disagree". [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L305-L316)

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L280-L331)

## Loading a Lightning Checkpoint with `load_for_prediction`

`deepspotm.load_for_prediction(checkpoint_path, ...)` is the workhorse for raw training-repo `.ckpt` files, including those containing a full `hyper_parameters` record. In its plain mode (no `token_path`/`gene_embeddings_path`), it delegates to Lightning's `DeepSpotM.load_from_checkpoint(..., map_location="cpu", strict=False)` — hyperparameters are restored from the checkpoint automatically because the constructor calls `save_hyperparameters()` — and then resolves the active source (see [Source Selection at Load Time](#source-selection-at-load-time) below). [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L160-L178)

Regardless of mode, every path through `load_for_prediction` finishes with the same normalization sequence: `model.to(device).eval()`, then `set_eval_transforms(center_crop=True)`, then return `(model, model.backbone.transforms)`. This is why every loader in the library hands back a *pair*: the `image_processor` is the backbone's own transform callable, already switched to the evaluation regime — the same object you stack image tiles against in the prediction loop. [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L180-L182), [predict.py](examples/predict.py#L130-L134)

> [!TIP]
> Device selection is centralized: both `from_pretrained` and `load_for_prediction` default to `cuda` when available, falling back to `cpu` — you only need to pass `device=` explicitly for deterministic placement. Also note that loading happens on `map_location="cpu"` in every branch; tensors are moved to the target device only in the final normalization step, which keeps peak host memory predictable.

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L116-L182)

## State-Dict Integrity Guards

The loading layer enforces a strict no-silent-drift policy through three exported utilities. The premise is stated in the guard's own docstring: weights the model expects but the checkpoint omitted (`missing`), or checkpoint keys the model lacks (`unexpected`), indicate the runtime model and the checkpoint disagree — and unaccounted drift "would silently use uninitialised weights, which is exactly the case we want to surface." [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L57-L71)

| Utility | Signature contract | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `filter_state_dict` | `(state_dict, drop_prefixes)` | Returns a copy with any key starting with a dropped prefix removed; empty prefixes yield an equal but distinct dict |
| `check_state_dict_load` | `(missing, unexpected, *, allow_missing_prefixes, allow_unexpected_prefixes)` | Raises `RuntimeError` listing counts and example keys for any drift outside the allow lists |
| `VOCAB_SPECIFIC_PREFIXES` | `("gene_decoder.gene_embeddings", "gene_decoder._router_bio_emb")` | The canonical allow/drop list for keys whose shape is tied to the gene vocabulary |

All three are part of the public API surface exported from `deepspotm`. [__init__.py](src/deepspotm/__init__.py#L10-L30)

The test suite pins the guard's semantics deliberately, because — as the test module puts it — "a regression in it fails quietly and looks like a bad model rather than a bad load." The tests cover clean loads, rejection of drift in either direction, prefix-filter removal semantics, copy-not-mutate behavior, and that declared allow-lists are honoured. [test_checkpoint.py](tests/test_checkpoint.py#L1-L6)

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L50-L86), [test_checkpoint.py](tests/test_checkpoint.py#L24-L68)

## The LoRA Wrap Contract During Loading

When `use_lora=True`, the backbone is wrapped by PEFT (`PeftModel` → `LoraModel` → `ImageEncoder`), so every backbone state-dict key carries the `backbone.base_model.model.` prefix and LoRA adapters sit alongside it in the same namespace. The contract — and this is the invariant that trips up most custom inference code — is to keep LoRA *wrapped* at predict time, in `forward`, in `predict_genes`, and inside `load_for_prediction`. [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L22-L31)

> [!TIP]
> Never call `model.backbone.merge_and_unload()` in the inference path. Doing so silently breaks the load-side round-trip: a freshly constructed `DeepSpotM(use_lora=True)` expects the PEFT-prefixed keys, so merged weights will match nothing and `strict=False`-style loads will drop them. Merge only if you fully control both the export and the load-side construction.

This prefixing is why `from_pretrained`'s drift filter exempts keys containing `lora`: a clean export may omit adapter bookkeeping buffers, but the adapter weights themselves still load into the wrapped structure. The eval-transform helper `set_eval_transforms` is also PEFT-aware — it walks the `base_model` → `model` delegation chain explicitly rather than relying on `__getattr__`, so a future PEFT release that breaks the chain cannot silently regress to a no-op. [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L352-L365)

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L22-L36), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L305-L311)

## Source Selection at Load Time

Multi-source checkpoints (five default sources: `evo2`, `orthrus`, `prott5`, `scgpt`, `apertus`) carry one gene-embedding bank and one adapter per source, and the active pathway is a **runtime-only decision**: "the selection is not persisted in `state_dict`, so freshly loaded checkpoints start with no active source." This makes `set_source()` a mandatory post-load step for any multi-source model, and explains why `current_source` returns `None` both for single-source models and for freshly loaded multi-source checkpoints. [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L196-L211), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L340-L350)

All three loaders encode the same resolution policy, differing only in where the source list is read from:

| Situation | `load_for_prediction` / `from_pretrained` behavior |
|---|---|
| Single-source checkpoint, no `source` arg | Source auto-inferred; `set_source` is effectively a consistency check |
| Multi-source checkpoint, `source=` given | Validated against the checkpoint's source list, then selected via `set_source` |
| Multi-source checkpoint, no `source` arg | Raises `ValueError` naming the available sources |
| Unknown `source` name | Raises `ValueError` listing the checkpoint's available sources |

For `load_for_prediction`'s plain mode, resolution happens after Lightning load against `model.sources`; for `from_pretrained`, after the safetensors load against the same property. The validation-and-collapse sequence is identical in spirit to the cross-vocab branch's earlier validation at [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L126-L143). Note that if you are loading a multi-source checkpoint under memory pressure, [DeepSpotM.load_for_inference](#loading-entry-points-at-a-glance) goes further and skips constructing the unused banks entirely — the full mechanics live on [Memory-Efficient Source Loading](15-memory-efficient-source-loading).

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L160-L178), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L213-L249), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L318-L327), [predict.py](examples/predict.py#L62-L65)

## Where to Go Next

Loading is deliberately the boundary between artifacts and inference. Depending on your goal, continue with:

- **Custom gene vocabularies** — the `token_path`/`gene_embeddings_path` swap branch of `load_for_prediction`, `swap_gene_vocabulary()`, and the prefix-drop algebra behind it: [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling)
- **Skipping unused source banks entirely** — how `load_for_inference` overrides `init_gene_embeddings` before construction to avoid materializing ~750 MB of unneeded embeddings: [Memory-Efficient Source Loading](15-memory-efficient-source-loading)
- **What the loaded model does next** — restricting predictions to a gene subset with `predict_genes`: [Selective Gene Prediction](16-selective-gene-prediction)
- **Why the state dict looks the way it does** — the PEFT wrapping and adapter targeting that produce the `backbone.base_model.model.` prefixes: [LoRA Adaptation Contract](8-lora-adaptation-contract)
- **Running it end to end** — the CLI that wraps `from_pretrained`: [Command-Line Prediction Tools](3-command-line-prediction-tools)

# Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling



This page documents the mechanism that lets a DeepSpotM checkpoint trained against one gene vocabulary be loaded into a model targeting a different vocabulary — a custom gene panel, or a cross-species retarget such as human-orthrus (~20k genes) → mouse-orthrus (74,815 genes). The design rests on three cooperating pieces: a classification of which state-dict keys are *vocabulary-shaped*, a weight-preserving vocabulary swap that runs *before* weight loading, and a strict drift guard that converts `strict=False` loading into an explicit, auditable allow-list. All of this is centralized in `checkpoint.py` and exported from the package's public API.

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L1-L23), [__init__.py](src/deepspotm/__init__.py#L10-L15)

## Why Checkpoints and Vocabularies Diverge

Every DeepSpotM model is built against an expression vocabulary: the packaged default `tokens.csv` (resolved via `config.ALPHABET_PATH`) unless a `token_path` hyperparameter overrides it. The decoder's cross-attention weight matrices, the vision backbone, and the LoRA adapters are all independent of the vocabulary size — but the gene-query embedding table and the biological-prior buffer are literally sized by it, and the output head (router or shared linear) is shaped by `bio_dim`. Loading a checkpoint whose vocabulary differs therefore cannot be a plain `load_state_dict`: the vocabulary-shaped tensors are incompatible by construction, and the temptation to silently drop them is exactly what the rest of this page guards against.

Sources: [config.py](src/deepspotm/config.py#L8-L16), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L72-L79), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L592-L602)

The following concept map distinguishes the two weight classes before we examine the load protocol. **Vocabulary-agnostic** weights transfer between vocabularies unchanged; **vocabulary-shaped** weights must be either freshly installed (via the swap) or explicitly excluded from the state dict.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Shared["Vocabulary-agnostic weights - load unchanged"]
        BB["backbone + LoRA adapters"]
        PP["gene_decoder.patch_proj"]
        CA["gene_decoder.layers.* cross-attention"]
    end
    subgraph Shaped["Vocabulary-shaped weights - depend on n_genes or bio_dim"]
        GE["gene_decoder.gene_embeddings - n_genes rows"]
        RB["gene_decoder._router_bio_emb buffer - n_genes rows"]
        RP["gene_decoder.gene_query_proj - input bio_dim"]
        RT["gene_decoder.router.* - input bio_dim"]
        MS["multi_source.bio_X / adapters.X / routers.X"]
    end
    Shared -. transfers across vocabularies .-> CKPT["Cross-vocab checkpoint"]
    Shaped -. filtered before load .-> CKPT
```

The full inventory, with the state-dict key each layer occupies and what drives its shape, is the foundation for every filtering decision downstream:

| Layer | State-dict key | Shape driver | Vocabulary sensitivity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gene query embedding | `gene_decoder.gene_embeddings.weight` | `(n_genes, bio_dim)` | Rows = vocabulary size |
| Router bio-prior buffer | `gene_decoder._router_bio_emb` | `(n_genes, bio_dim)` | Rows = vocabulary size |
| Query projection | `gene_decoder.gene_query_proj` | `bio_dim → gene_embed_dim` | Input dim only (`bio_dim`) |
| Router MLPs (`weight_net`, `bias_net`) | `gene_decoder.router.*` | `bio_dim → hidden → D / 1` | Input dim only |
| Multi-source bio bank | `gene_decoder.multi_source.bio_<source>` | `(n_genes, bio_dim_i)` | Rows = vocabulary size |
| Multi-source adapters | `gene_decoder.multi_source.adapters.<source>.*` | `bio_dim_i → gene_embed_dim` | `bio_dim_i` only |
| Per-source routers | `gene_decoder.routers.<source>.*` | `bio_dim_i → …` | `bio_dim_i` only |
| Backbone / LoRA / `patch_proj` / attention | `backbone.*`, `gene_decoder.patch_proj`, `gene_decoder.layers.*` | Architecture hparams | None |

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L16-L23), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L514-L602), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L183-L234)

## The Build–Swap–Load Protocol

The entry point for cross-vocabulary loading is `load_for_prediction`. Its contract, stated in the module docstring, is deliberate about ordering: **construct with the default vocabulary, swap the gene decoder to the target vocabulary, then load the checkpoint with vocab-specific keys filtered out.** The protocol proceeds as follows (prerequisite: a Lightning `.ckpt` whose `hyper_parameters` describe the training-time architecture, plus the target vocabulary's `tokens.csv` and a `(n_genes_new, bio_dim)` embedding tensor):

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["torch.load checkpoint - extract hyper_parameters"] --> B["hparams['token_path'] = None - force default vocabulary"]
    B --> C["DeepSpotM hparams - init-time shape asserts pass"]
    C --> D["model.swap_gene_vocabulary - retarget to target vocab"]
    D --> E{"hparams['init_gene_embeddings'] is a list?"}
    E -->|yes| F["_multi_source_drop_prefixes - collapse to source"]
    E -->|no| G["VOCAB_SPECIFIC_PREFIXES"]
    F --> H["filter_state_dict on ckpt state_dict"]
    G --> H
    H --> I["model.load_state_dict strict=False"]
    I --> J["check_state_dict_load - allow only filtered prefixes as missing"]
    J --> K["model.eval + set_eval_transforms center_crop"]
```

Cross-vocab mode activates when *both* `token_path` and `gene_embeddings_path` are supplied. The checkpoint's hyperparameters are read eagerly with `torch.load(..., weights_only=False)`, and `hparams["token_path"]` is forced to `None` so the model builds against the packaged default vocabulary rather than the checkpoint's (custom) one. Only then does `model.swap_gene_vocabulary(gene_embeddings_path, token_path, source=...)` retarget the decoder in place, after which the state dict is filtered, loaded with `strict=False`, and validated. The function returns `(model, image_processor)` with the model on device, in eval mode, and the backbone switched to center-crop inference transforms.

> [!TIP]
> Constructing with the default vocabulary first is not incidental — it is required for the swap to be reachable. `CrossAttentionGeneDecoder.__init__` asserts that a registry-loaded bio embedding's row count equals `n_genes`; building directly with a custom `token_path` would pair a custom-sized vocabulary with default-sized registry embeddings and fail that assert at construction. Building default-first defers all vocabulary retargeting to `swap_vocabulary`, which is built to handle it.

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L89-L148), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L180-L182), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L566-L578)

## Vocabulary-Shaped Keys and the Drift Guard

`VOCAB_SPECIFIC_PREFIXES` names exactly the two single-source tensors whose *row count* is tied to the training vocabulary: `gene_decoder.gene_embeddings` and `gene_decoder._router_bio_emb`. These are dropped from the checkpoint's state dict because `swap_vocabulary` has already installed fresh, target-vocabulary versions of both — reloading the checkpoint's stale-shaped copies would either fail or overwrite the swap.

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L16-L23)

| Filtering scenario | Dropped prefixes | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Single-source cross-vocab | `gene_decoder.gene_embeddings`, `gene_decoder._router_bio_emb` | Rows are checkpoint-vocab-shaped; fresh copies installed by the swap |
| Multi-source cross-vocab keeping source *S* | `gene_decoder.multi_source.bio_S`; plus `bio_X`, `adapters.X.*`, `routers.X.*` for every *X* ≠ *S* | Kept bank changes shape with the new vocab; other sources no longer exist on the collapsed model |

`filter_state_dict` performs prefix-based key removal and returns a **copy** — the input state dict is never mutated (a contract pinned by `test_filter_state_dict_without_prefixes_is_a_copy`). Because filtered keys are now legitimately missing from the state dict, the load must use `strict=False`; that flag alone would also swallow *accidental* drift, so `check_state_dict_load` re-implements strictness with explicit allow-lists: any missing or unexpected key that does not start with a declared prefix raises `RuntimeError` reporting counts and examples. The stated rationale in both the guard's docstring and the test module is that the alternative failure mode — predictions silently produced by uninitialized weights — *looks like a bad model rather than a bad load*, and is therefore worth failing fast on.

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L26-L86), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L150-L159), [test_checkpoint.py](tests/test_checkpoint.py#L1-L45)

The guard's behavior is directly pinned by the test suite (see [Test Suite and Packaging](19-test-suite-and-packaging)):

| Test | Verified behavior |
|---|---|
| `test_filter_state_dict_drops_matching_prefixes` | Vocab-shaped keys removed; shared keys (e.g. `image_encoder.blocks.*`) kept |
| `test_filter_state_dict_without_prefixes_is_a_copy` | No-mutation contract |
| `test_check_state_dict_load_accepts_clean_load` | Zero drift passes |
| `test_check_state_dict_load_rejects_unexplained_drift` | Missing *or* unexpected keys outside allow lists raise `RuntimeError("unaccounted-for key drift")` |
| `test_check_state_dict_load_honours_allow_lists` | Drift the caller declared expected is permitted |
| `test_vocab_specific_prefixes_shape` | The prefix registry is a non-empty tuple of strings |

Sources: [test_checkpoint.py](tests/test_checkpoint.py#L17-L68)

> [!TIP]
> Note what the guard deliberately does *not* allow-list: the router MLP weights (`gene_decoder.router.*`) and `gene_query_proj`. Their shapes depend only on `bio_dim`, so the supported cross-vocabulary scenarios in this codebase are `bio_dim`-preserving swaps (orthrus 512-d, prott5 1024-d — only `n_genes` changes), under which those checkpoint weights load intact and are reused. If `bio_dim` were to change, those tensors could no longer reconcile with the freshly swapped model, and the drift surfaces as an explicit error instead of a silent reinitialization.

## Weight-Preserving Swap Semantics

The swap itself — `CrossAttentionGeneDecoder.swap_vocabulary` — is engineered around a single principle: **rebuild only what the new vocabulary's shape forces; preserve trained weights everywhere else.** On the single-source path, `gene_embeddings` is always replaced (the vocabulary's content changed by definition). `gene_query_proj` is rebuilt *only* when the new `bio_dim` differs from both the embedding dim and the current projection's input features — the code cites the `prott5 → mouse-prott5` case (both 1024-d) as the scenario where the trained projection survives. The router is rebuilt only when it is absent or its input `bio_dim` changes, inheriting the existing router's hidden dim when present; switching output-head representations in either direction (shared `Linear(gene_embed_dim, 1)` ↔ router hypernetwork) is supported, with the stale side's module and buffer deleted to keep the state-dict surface clean.

| Component | Swap action | Preservation rule |
|---|---|---|
| `gene_embeddings` | Always rebuilt from new bio embeddings | Never preserved (vocab content changed) |
| `gene_query_proj` | Rebuilt only if required input dim differs | Preserved when `bio_dim` unchanged |
| `router` + `_router_bio_emb` | Router rebuilt only when absent or input `bio_dim` changes; buffer always refreshed | MLP weights preserved when `bio_dim` unchanged |
| Shared `output_proj` ↔ router | Both transition directions supported; stale side deleted | Never cross-preserved |
| Multi-source decoder | `collapse_to_source`: prune other sources, re-register kept bio parameter | Kept adapter + router preserved verbatim when `bio_dim` matches |

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L608-L711), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L666-L678)

At the model level, `DeepSpotM.swap_gene_vocabulary` wraps this with vocabulary-file I/O and validation: it reads the target `tokens.csv`, filters `token_type == 'gene'` rows, loads the embedding tensor with `weights_only=True`, and rejects any row-count/list-length mismatch with a `ValueError` *before* touching the decoder. It then updates `n_genes`, propagates an explicit `use_router` override into the hyperparameters, and returns the ordered gene-name list — which becomes the authoritative mapping for interpreting output columns under the new vocabulary (for the general mapping machinery, see [Gene Vocabulary and Output Mapping](12-gene-vocabulary-and-output-mapping) and [Selective Gene Prediction](16-selective-gene-prediction)).

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L126-L191), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L1-L32)

## Multi-Source Collapse at Load Time

When the checkpoint declares a multi-source decoder (`init_gene_embeddings` is a list of source names from the registry spanning evo2, orthrus, prott5, scgpt, apertus, and others), cross-vocab loading requires a `source` argument naming which pathway survives. `_multi_source_drop_prefixes` builds the exclusion set: the *kept* source's `bio_{S}` bank (its rows change with the new vocabulary), plus every other source's `bio_{X}`, `adapters.X.*`, and `routers.X.*` (those parameters do not exist on the collapsed model). The swap itself delegates to `MultiSourceGeneEmbedding.collapse_to_source`, which enforces the load-bearing invariant: **the new vocabulary's `bio_dim` must equal the kept source's existing adapter input dim**, so the trained adapter `Linear` and the per-source router (see [Gene Router Hypernetwork](10-gene-router-hypernetwork), [Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings)) are preserved verbatim while `n_genes` changes freely.

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L26-L47), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L126-L153), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L333-L385)

Source resolution is strict but forgiving of the already-collapsed case: a single-element `init_gene_embeddings` list lets `load_for_prediction` infer the source; a multi-element list raises `ValueError` if `source` is omitted or names an unknown pathway. Two round-trip details close the loop. First, `collapse_to_source` sets `active_source` immediately, so the collapsed model is forward-ready without a separate `set_source` call. Second, `swap_gene_vocabulary` rewrites `hparams["init_gene_embeddings"]` to `[source]`, so if the retargeted model is later re-serialized, `load_from_checkpoint` rebuilds the same collapsed structure — the collapse is durable across checkpoint generations, not just a load-time trick. This contrasts with the non-cross-vocab multi-source path, where `active_source` is a plain Python attribute excluded from the state dict and must be selected via `set_source` after load; for the memory-oriented variant of that path, see [Memory-Efficient Source Loading](15-memory-efficient-source-loading).

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L126-L143), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L160-L178), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L184-L190), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L175-L181), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L639-L655)

The interaction structure across the three modules involved is:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    LFP["checkpoint.load_for_prediction"] --> SGV["model.DeepSpotM.swap_gene_vocabulary"]
    SGV --> SV["modules.CrossAttentionGeneDecoder.swap_vocabulary"]
    SV --> CTS["modules.MultiSourceGeneEmbedding.collapse_to_source"]
    LFP --> FSD["checkpoint.filter_state_dict"]
    LFP --> GUARD["checkpoint.check_state_dict_load"]
    LFP --> SS["model.DeepSpotM.set_source - non-cross-vocab path"]
```

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L89-L182), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L126-L211), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L608-L711)

## Choosing the Right Loader

For a raw Lightning checkpoint with a non-default target vocabulary, the cross-vocab path is one call:

```python
from deepspotm import load_for_prediction

model, image_processor = load_for_prediction(
    "strs_mouse.ckpt",
    token_path="mouse_tokens.csv",            # target vocabulary (gene rows)
    gene_embeddings_path="mouse_orthrus.pt",  # (74815, 512) bio embeddings
    source="orthrus",                         # required for multi-source checkpoints
)
```

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L89-L115), [__init__.py](src/deepspotm/__init__.py#L10-L15)

`load_for_prediction` is one of four loading surfaces; the matrix below positions it against the alternatives. Note that `from_pretrained` (published safetensors, default vocabulary) and `load_for_inference` (bank-skipping multi-source load) solve different problems and are covered in [Pretrained Model Loading](13-pretrained-model-loading) and [Memory-Efficient Source Loading](15-memory-efficient-source-loading) respectively.

| API | Input artifact | Cross-vocab support | Multi-source handling | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `load_for_prediction` | Lightning `.ckpt` | Yes — `token_path` + `gene_embeddings_path` | Collapse to one `source` at load | Training checkpoints retargeted to another vocabulary |
| `DeepSpotM.swap_gene_vocabulary` | A constructed model | Yes — in-place retarget | `source` arg collapses the model | Retargeting a live model already in memory |
| `DeepSpotM.from_pretrained` | `config.json` + `model.safetensors` + `tokens.csv` | No (default vocabulary) | `set_source` selection | Published models |
| `DeepSpotM.load_for_inference` | Lightning `.ckpt` | No | `source` override skips unused banks | Memory-constrained multi-source inference |

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L89-L182), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L213-L331)

## Failure Modes This Design Eliminates

The architecture closes three specific silent-failure channels. First, *stale-shaped overwrite*: vocabulary-shaped checkpoint tensors are filtered before load, so a cross-vocab load can never clobber the freshly swapped embeddings or bio buffer. Second, *uninitialized-weight prediction*: because filtering forces `strict=False`, the drift guard restores strictness with explicit allow-lists — any key drift outside the declared prefixes raises with diagnostics rather than degrading quietly. Third, *lost collapse state*: the hyperparameter rewrite to `[source]` and the immediate `active_source` assignment mean a collapsed, cross-vocab model round-trips through save/load and is forward-ready without hidden post-load state. These guarantees, and the tests that pin them, are the reason cross-vocabulary prediction can be treated as a first-class supported operation rather than a best-effort hack — for the decoder internals being retargeted, continue with [Cross-Attention Gene Decoder](9-cross-attention-gene-decoder), and for the attention mechanics underlying gene queries, see the decoder's interaction with [Gene Router Hypernetwork](10-gene-router-hypernetwork).


# Memory-Efficient Source Loading



DeepSpotM checkpoints can carry a **multi-source gene decoder** — one biological gene-embedding bank, one projection adapter, and one hypernetwork router per source (evo2, orthrus, prott5, scgpt, apertus, …). At inference time, however, only *one* of those sources ever fires. This page explains the loading machinery that exploits that asymmetry: how `load_for_inference(source=...)` and `from_pretrained(source=...)` build the model with a single source's parameters, skip reading the raw gene-embedding `.pt` assets entirely, and verify that nothing substantive was silently dropped in the process. For the architecture of the multi-source decoder itself, see [Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings); for the general `from_pretrained` entry point, see [Pretrained Model Loading](13-pretrained-model-loading).

## The Problem: Five Sources Loaded, One Source Used

A multi-source checkpoint's `state_dict` is dominated by per-source payloads. Each source contributes a trainable `bio_{source}` gene-token bank of shape `(n_genes, bio_dim_i)`, an adapter (`Linear(bio_dim_i → gene_embed_dim)` + `LayerNorm`), and — when routing is enabled — a `GeneRouter` hypernetwork. The five default sources total roughly **750 MB on disk** before you count the vision backbone, yet inference dispatches on a single `active_source` string per forward pass ([Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings)).

The loading trap comes from how `active_source` is stored. It is deliberately a *plain Python attribute, not a buffer or parameter*, so it never appears in `state_dict` and cannot survive a checkpoint round-trip. A freshly loaded multi-source model has no active source until you set one explicitly — and a naive `load_from_checkpoint` materializes **all five** source banks into RAM whether or not you will ever touch four of them.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L216-L229), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L174-L181), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L242-L244)

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph CKPT["Multi-source checkpoint (~750 MB of sources)"]
        B1["bio_evo2 + adapter + router"]
        B2["bio_orthrus + adapter + router"]
        B3["bio_prott5 + adapter + router"]
        B4["bio_scgpt + adapter + router"]
        B5["bio_apertus + adapter + router"]
    end
    subgraph NAIVE["Naive load_from_checkpoint"]
        M1["All 5 banks materialized in RAM"]
        M2["4 sources: dead weight"]
    end
    subgraph EFF["load_for_inference(source='scgpt')"]
        E1["Only bio_scgpt bank + adapter + router built"]
        E2["Other 4 sources' tensors dropped via strict=False"]
    end
    CKPT --> NAIVE
    CKPT --> EFF
    NAIVE -. "wasted RAM + .pt file I/O" .-> M2
    EFF ==>|"one source kept"| E1
```

## The Primary Mechanism: `load_for_inference(source=...)`

`DeepSpotM.load_for_inference` is the inference-optimized loader that makes source collapse a one-argument operation. When `source` is passed, it executes a three-step contract documented in its docstring: **(1)** it overrides the checkpoint's `init_gene_embeddings` hyperparameter to `[source]`, so the decoder constructs a `MultiSourceGeneEmbedding` holding *only* that source's bank and adapter — the embedding registry opens just that one `.pt` file; **(2)** it loads the checkpoint `state_dict` with `strict=False`, so the unused sources' tensors are silently dropped instead of raising key-mismatch errors; **(3)** it calls `set_source(source)` so the model is immediately forward-ready despite `active_source` not persisting through the round-trip.

The method is deliberately conservative at its boundary: for a **single-source** checkpoint you must omit `source` (it then delegates to `load_from_checkpoint` unchanged), and passing `source` to a single-source checkpoint raises a `RuntimeError` *after* load. The guard exists because the single-source layout stores the bio weights as a `bio_emb` buffer rather than a per-source `bio_<name>` parameter — under `strict=False` that mismatch would silently discard the actual trained bio weights, so the loader surfaces it explicitly instead.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L213-L249), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L196-L211)

> [!TIP]
> The `strict=False` in step 2 is scoped and intentional — it is what permits the key-set mismatch between a five-source checkpoint and a one-source runtime model. Every other loading path in the codebase pairs `strict=False` with an explicit drift check (below), so "strict=False" here is never a license for silent weight loss on the *kept* source.

## Building by Shape, Not by File: `from_shapes` vs `from_registry`

The memory savings above are powered by a constructor-level choice inside `CrossAttentionGeneDecoder`. When `init_gene_embeddings` is a list, the decoder picks between two builders:

- **`from_registry`** (training-time default): iterates the source names through `_GENE_EMB_LOADERS`, which opens each `deepspotm.assets/*.pt` file via `importlib.resources` and `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)`, then copies the raw biological prior into each trainable `bio_{source}` parameter.
- **`from_shapes`** (checkpoint-loading path): receives only a `bio_dims` dict mapping each source name to its embedding width, and allocates **zero-initialized** tensors of the right `(n_genes, bio_dim)` shapes. The raw `.pt` assets are never opened — the docstring is explicit that the trained `bio_{source}` values arrive via `load_state_dict` and overwrite the zeros.

The decoder switches on one signal: if `bio_dims` is provided, it takes the shape path; otherwise it hits the registry. This is why `bio_dims` is described in the model's hyperparameters as *derived metadata, not state* — adapter input shapes carry the same information and a strict load would catch any disagreement — but storing it in `config.json` lets a published checkpoint reconstruct its parameter geometry without shipping or reading eleven embedding files.

Sources: [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L528-L546), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L306-L324), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L282-L304), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L214-L226), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L458-L470), [modules.py](src/deepspotm/modules.py#L95-L104)

| Dimension | `from_registry` | `from_shapes` |
|---|---|---|
| Input data | Source name list → opens each `assets/*.pt` | `bio_dims` dict from `config.json` only |
| File I/O at build | One `.pt` read per source (up to 11 registered) | **Zero** asset reads |
| Initial `bio_*` values | Raw biological prior (`weights_only=True` load) | Zeros, overwritten by `load_state_dict` |
| Used when | Training-time construction | Any checkpoint load with `bio_dims` set |
| Failure mode | `FileNotFoundError` naming the missing asset | Shape mismatch caught by load-drift checks |

## The Full Picture: `from_pretrained` Source Selection

`DeepSpotM.from_pretrained` composes all of these techniques into the published-artifact loading path. It reads `config.json` for hyperparameters (including `bio_dims`), then performs two memory-relevant overrides before constructing the model: it injects `token_path` from the repo's `tokens.csv` and forces `backbone_pretrained=False`, so the vision backbone is built as *bare architecture* without downloading its upstream weights — those arrive from `model.safetensors` instead, making the load fully offline. The decoder then takes the `from_shapes` branch, allocating `bio_*` parameters by shape alone.

Weights are read with `safetensors.torch.load_file`, which memory-maps the serialized tensors rather than eagerly materializing a full `torch.load` pickle. The load uses `strict=False` paired with a **targeted drift check**: missing keys are only tolerated in LoRA/PEFT bookkeeping namespaces (any key containing `lora`, case-insensitive), while a missing key under `gene_decoder.` or `backbone.` raises a `RuntimeError` declaring that the config and weights disagree. This mirrors the guard philosophy in [Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling): relax strictness precisely where a structural difference is expected, and audit everything else.

Finally, source selection runs on the reconstructed model. If `model.sources` is a single source, it is inferred automatically; a multi-source model demands `source=` explicitly and raises `ValueError` if omitted; then `set_source(source)` arms the dispatch. The CLI wraps this end-to-end — `examples/predict.py` exposes `--source` with the five default choices and calls `DeepSpotM.from_pretrained(args.repo, source=args.source)`.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L251-L331), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L57-L66), [image_encoder.py](src/deepspotm/image_encoder.py#L43-L52), [examples/predict.py](examples/predict.py#L62-L65), [examples/predict.py](examples/predict.py#L156-L162)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["from_pretrained(repo, source=?)"] --> B{"Local dir or HF repo?"}
    B -->|dir| C["Read config.json / model.safetensors / tokens.csv"]
    B -->|repo id| D["hf_hub_download all three"]
    C --> E["hparams: token_path set,<br/>backbone_pretrained=False"]
    D --> E
    E --> F["DeepSpotM(**hparams)<br/>→ decoder uses from_shapes(bio_dims)<br/>→ no .pt assets, no backbone download"]
    F --> G["state_dict = safetensors load_file<br/>(memory-mapped)"]
    G --> H["load_state_dict strict=False"]
    H --> I{"Missing keys under<br/>gene_decoder. / backbone.<br/>and not lora?"}
    I -->|yes| J["RuntimeError: config/weights disagree"]
    I -->|no| K{"model.sources"}
    K -->|"1 source"| L["Infer source"]
    K -->|">1, source given"| L
    K -->|">1, source=None"| M["ValueError: source required"]
    L --> N["set_source → model armed for forward"]
```

> [!TIP]
> Reading `from_shapes`' zero-init parameters through a safetensors mmap means the peak memory cost of the unused-source path is never paid at *any* stage — not at parameter allocation (zeros are cheap placeholders of the right shape), not at file I/O (only the checkpoint you asked for is opened), and not at load time (`strict=False` drops foreign keys before they are bound to modules).

## The Cross-Vocab Collapse Filter

A second, related collapse mechanism lives in `checkpoint.py` for the cross-vocabulary flow. When `load_for_prediction` detects a multi-source checkpoint (its saved `init_gene_embeddings` is a list), it requires a `source` argument and builds a set of state-dict prefixes to drop via `_multi_source_drop_prefixes`: the kept source's `bio_{kept}` (whose shape is about to change under the vocabulary swap) plus *every* other source's `bio_{other}`, `adapters.{other}.*`, and `routers.{other}.*` — parameters that no longer exist on the collapsed model. `filter_state_dict` then strips matching keys, and `check_state_dict_load` validates that `load_state_dict`'s missing/unexpected key reports fall exactly within the declared allow lists, raising a `RuntimeError` naming sample keys on any unexplained drift.

This is the same "filter, load, then audit" pattern as `load_for_inference`, applied one level up: instead of *not building* the unused sources, the cross-vocab path builds the full default-vocab model first (so init-time asserts pass), swaps the vocabulary, and *filters out* the collapsed parameters before binding. The unit tests pin the filter semantics: dropped prefixes remove exactly the matching keys and everything else survives; an empty prefix list yields an equal-but-distinct copy.

Sources: [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L26-L47), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L50-L54), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L57-L86), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L121-L159), [tests/test_checkpoint.py](tests/test_checkpoint.py#L24-L32)

## Choosing the Right Loader

| Entry point | Memory behavior | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| `DeepSpotM.from_pretrained(repo, source=…)` | Shape-built sources, safetensors mmap, offline backbone, single source armed | Loading a published HF repo or export dir — the default inference path |
| `DeepSpotM.load_for_inference(ckpt, source=…)` | Skips unused multi-source banks; registry opens one `.pt` only | Loading a raw Lightning `.ckpt` for single-source inference |
| `DeepSpotM.load_from_checkpoint(ckpt)` | Materializes *all* sources of a multi-source checkpoint | Reproducing training state, or single-source checkpoints |
| `checkpoint.load_for_prediction(ckpt, …, source=…)` | Prefix-filtered collapse, required for cross-vocab multi-source loads | Custom-vocabulary prediction over a multi-source checkpoint ([Cross-Vocabulary Checkpoint Handling](14-cross-vocabulary-checkpoint-handling)) |

One safety property ties the loaders together: none of them trust `strict=False` alone. Every path either raises on source ambiguity before load, raises on missing substantive weights after load, or validates the missing/unexpected key reports against explicit allow lists. That is what makes "load less" safe rather than merely convenient — the weights you *do* load are guaranteed complete.

Sources: [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L238-L249), [model.py](src/deepspotm/model.py#L305-L316), [checkpoint.py](src/deepspotm/checkpoint.py#L156-L159)

**Where to go next**: for the runtime dispatch that `set_source` arms — how `active_source` selects the bank/adapter pair at forward time — see [Multi-Source Gene Embeddings](11-multi-source-gene-embeddings); for restricting the output panel itself, see [Selective Gene Prediction](16-selective-gene-prediction); for the CLI walkthrough built on this loader, see [Command-Line Prediction Tools](3-command-line-prediction-tools).

# Selective Gene Prediction



Selective gene prediction is DeepSpot-M's mechanism for computing expression values for an **arbitrary subset of genes** — by symbol or by index — instead of always evaluating the full vocabulary. This page documents the three access levels (the `predict_genes` convenience API, the raw `forward(gene_indices=...)` path, and the CLI `--genes` flag), the decoder-level mechanics that make subsetting a genuine compute reduction rather than a post-hoc slice, and the behavioral contract verified by the test suite. It assumes familiarity with the decoder architecture described in [Cross-Attention Gene Decoder](9-cross-attention-gene-decoder).

## Why Subsetting Works: Queries, Not Outputs

The key architectural insight is that DeepSpot-M's decoder generates **per-gene queries** from biological gene embeddings, then lets each query cross-attend to the image's patch tokens. Because genes enter the computation as independently constructed query vectors, a subset request can be applied at *query construction time* — the selected queries are built, attended, and projected, and the unselected ones are never materialized. Contrast this with a conventional fixed output head (a single `Linear(hidden, n_genes)` matrix), where the full panel must be computed first and the subset can only be extracted afterward.

This is exactly the split you see in `DeepSpotM.forward`: with the cross-attention decoder, `gene_indices` flows down into the decoder and reduces work; with the legacy MLP `gene_head`, the full panel is computed and the result is post-hoc `index_select`-ed.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
```
